title: Add user and assign platform role
t1: Add the business user to your Experience Platform product profile in Adobe Admin Console to grant them system access.
t2: Assign the user a role in the Experience Platform Permissions UI to control which features and data they can access.

title: Add user and assign sandbox permissions
t1: Add the marketer as a user in the Admin Console to grant them access to the Experience Platform organization.
t2: Assign the marketer a role in the Permissions UI that includes access to the required sandboxes and audience-builder features.

title: Create role and provision analyst
t1: Create a read-only reporting role in the Permissions UI with view-only access to datasets, segments, and dashboards.
t2: Add the new data analyst user in Admin Console and assign them the read-only reporting role so they can access reports without edit rights.

title: Add user and assign journey permissions
t1: Add the user to your Adobe organization in the Admin Console so they can access Experience Platform.
t2: Assign the Journey Optimizer journey-authoring role to the user in the Permissions UI to grant the correct access.

title: Grant developer access to Platform APIs
t1: Add the developer to your Experience Platform product profile in the Adobe Admin Console to grant them access.
t2: Assign the developer the required role and API credentials in the Permissions UI so they can authenticate and call Experience Platform APIs.

title: Grant developer API sandbox access
t1: Add the developer to your organization in the Admin Console and generate their API credentials for the desired project.
t2: Assign the developer's API credential to a role in the Permissions UI to grant the required sandbox and source access.

title: Grant developer API access to Sources and Destinations
t1: Add the data engineer as a developer in Adobe Admin Console so they can create API credentials for Experience Platform.
t2: Assign the developer a role in the Permissions UI that grants access to the Sources and Destinations APIs so they can make authorized programmatic calls.

title: Promote user to product admin
t1: In the Adobe Admin Console, locate the experienced Platform user and add them to the Experience Platform product administrator role.
t2: Confirm the user now appears under product admins so they can manage permissions, sandboxes, and configurations within Experience Platform.

title: Grant admin rights to team lead
t1: Add the platform team lead as a product administrator in the Adobe Admin Console to grant them access to the product.
t2: Assign the team lead an administrator role in the Experience Platform Permissions UI so they can manage permissions for their team.

title: Restrict PHI fields from agency users
t1: Apply attribute-based access control labels to protected health information schema fields to mark them as sensitive and restricted.
t2: Configure a role for external agency users that explicitly denies access to those labeled PHI fields, preventing them from viewing or activating that data.

title: Label PHI fields and restrict access
t1: Apply PHI data labels to sensitive health-related fields in your schema to mark them as restricted.
t2: Configure a role in the Permissions UI to block access to those labeled fields, preventing unauthorized users from viewing health data.

title: Label fields and enforce access policy
t1: Apply attribute-based access control labels to regulated financial PII schema fields to mark them as sensitive and restricted.
t2: Create an access policy that denies any role without explicit permissions from viewing or activating those labeled financial PII fields.

title: Label consent field and enforce access
t1: Apply a GDPR-restricted data usage label to the consent schema field to mark it as sensitive and limit visibility.
t2: Create a role-based access control policy that denies access to any field carrying that label, enforcing it across all assigned users.

title: Promote sandbox configs to production
t1: Create a development sandbox and build and test your configurations, schemas, and audiences within it.
t2: Package the validated configurations and publish them to the production sandbox for live use.

title: Test schema and ingestion in sandbox
t1: Create a development sandbox and build your new schema and ingestion pipeline inside it to test without affecting production data.
t2: Validate that data ingests correctly into the sandbox environment, then replicate the confirmed schema and pipeline configuration in the production sandbox.

title: Create and assign regional sandbox
t1: Create a new sandbox in the Admin Console and give it a name that identifies the regional business unit it will serve.
t2: Assign the appropriate users and roles to that sandbox so the regional team has access to their dedicated environment.

title: Create sandbox for playbooks exploration
t1: Create a new sandbox in the Admin UI and designate it as an inspiration sandbox for Use Case Playbooks exploration.
t2: Switch into the inspiration sandbox to browse and instantiate Use Case Playbooks without affecting production data.

title: Reset sandbox for fresh project start
t1: Navigate to the Sandboxes section in the Admin UI and select the development sandbox you want to clear between project phases.
t2: Trigger a sandbox reset to delete all assets, schemas, and data within it, leaving a clean environment ready for the next project phase.

title: Promote campaign config to production
t1: Package the tested campaign configuration in the development sandbox by selecting its assets and publishing the sandbox package.
t2: Import the published package into the production sandbox to deploy the campaign configuration exactly as tested.

title: Copy journey package to target sandbox
t1: In the source sandbox, create and publish a package containing the journey and all its dependent audience and schema assets.
t2: Import the published package into the target sandbox to automatically recreate the journey and its dependencies without manual configuration.

title: Migrate schemas from staging to production
t1: Package the validated schemas and datasets in the staging sandbox and publish the package so it is ready for export.
t2: Import the published package into the production sandbox to deploy the validated schemas and datasets.

title: Package and deploy audience activation flow
t1: Bundle all audience activation assets, including schemas, datasets, segments, and destinations, into a sandbox package in your development sandbox.
t2: Publish the package and import it into your production sandbox to deploy the complete audience activation flow.

title: Package schema and deploy to sandbox
t1: Create and publish a sandbox package containing the governance-approved data schema from the source sandbox.
t2: Import the published package into the target regional sandbox to deploy the schema there.

title: Share journey config with partner org
source: Sandbox Tooling / Share packages across orgs
t1: Package the customer success journey configuration, including schemas, datasets, and journey assets, into a sandbox package and publish it.
t2: Share the published package with the partner Adobe org and import it into their target sandbox to replicate the journey configuration.

title: Export compliance model to partner orgs
source: Sandbox Tooling / Share packages across orgs
t1: Publish a sandbox package containing the compliance-approved audience model, schemas, and datasets from the source IMS org.
t2: Import the published package into each target IMS org's sandbox to deploy the identical compliance-approved audience model across organizations.

title: Export and import cross-org campaign package
source: Sandbox Tooling / Share packages across orgs
t1: Publish the co-branded campaign configuration as a sandbox package in the source organization to make it available for sharing.
t2: Import the published package into the target organization's sandbox to replicate the campaign configuration across orgs.

title: Model loyalty data with profile schema
t1: Create an XDM Individual Profile schema for customer loyalty data and add identity fields such as email and loyalty ID to enable profile stitching.
t2: Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so ingested loyalty records are merged into unified customer profiles using those identity fields.

title: Create XDM Experience Event schema
t1: Create a new XDM Experience Event schema in the Schema Editor and add field groups that capture web clickstream behavior such as page views and link clicks.
t2: Save and enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so that ingested web clickstream events can be unified into customer profiles.

title: Mobile event schema with device identity
t1: Create an XDM Experience Event schema for mobile app interactions and add the Mobile SDK ExperienceEvent mixin to capture device identity fields such as IDFA and GAID.
t2: Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so that incoming mobile interaction events are stitched to unified profiles using those device identities.

title: Build B2C profile schema with identities
t1: Create an Individual Profile schema for your B2C brand and add email and CRM ID fields as primary and secondary identity descriptors.
t2: Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so ingested records merge into unified profiles using those identity fields.

title: Create in-store purchase event schema
t1: Create an XDM Experience Event schema and add field groups for commerce transaction details and loyalty program identifiers to capture in-store purchase data.
t2: Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile by designating the loyalty ID as the primary identity so purchase events can be stitched to unified customer profiles.

title: Add custom field group to schema
t1: Create a custom field group with subscription status fields and add it to the existing profile schema in the Schema Editor.
t2: Save the updated schema so the new subscription status fields are available for data ingestion and profile enrichment.

title: Add loyalty tier fields to profile schema
t1: Create a custom field group containing your company-specific loyalty tier attributes and add it to the standard Individual Profile schema.
t2: Save the updated schema so all datasets using it can capture and store the new loyalty tier fields in customer profiles.

title: Custom consent field group for GDPR
t1: Create a custom field group containing consent and preference fields, such as marketing opt-in status and data processing agreements, to capture GDPR-required information.
t2: Add the custom consent field group to your customer profile schema so that all ingested records carry the required GDPR consent and preference attributes.

title: Add propensity score field group to schema
t1: Create a custom field group containing AI propensity score attributes such as churn likelihood and purchase probability.
t2: Add the new field group to an existing XDM Individual Profile schema so those score attributes become available on customer profiles.

title: Define custom class for product entity
t1: Create a custom XDM class in the Schema Editor to define the new product entity type with its unique identifier and core behavior.
t2: Build a schema based on that custom class to capture the specific product attributes needed for your catalog.

title: Create reusable address type for schemas
t1: Define a reusable structured address data type containing fields like street, city, state, and postal code in the Schema Editor.
t2: Add the saved address data type as a field to both the profile schema and the order schema so they share a consistent address structure.

title: Link product catalog to profile schema
t1: Define a reference field on the product catalog schema that points to the primary identity of the customer profile schema.
t2: Configure a schema relationship using that reference field to formally link the product catalog schema to the customer profile schema.

title: Link order events to profile schema
t1: Define a relationship field on the order event schema that references the primary identity field of the profile schema.
t2: Configure the schema relationship in the Schema Editor to enable joining order event records to their corresponding profile records at query time.

title: Model B2B account and opportunity data
t1: Create a schema using the XDM Business Account class to model your B2B account data, capturing firmographic attributes and account identifiers.
t2: Create a second schema using the XDM Business Opportunity class and link it to the account schema to enable account-based marketing across related records.

title: Link Account and Contact B2B schemas
t1: Create an Account schema and a Contact schema in Experience Platform using the XDM Business Account and XDM Business Contact classes.
t2: Define a relationship field on the Contact schema that references the Account schema's primary identity to establish the B2B account-contact link.

title: Copy production schema to regional sandbox
t1: Export the finalized production schema, including all its field groups, by packaging it from the source sandbox.
t2: Import the packaged schema into the target regional sandbox to recreate the complete schema structure there.

title: Add consent field to profile schema
t1: Open the existing customer profile schema in the Schema Editor and add a new opt-in consent field using the appropriate consent data type.
t2: Save the updated schema so that all datasets built on it can capture and enforce the new consent field going forward.

title: Add custom field group to schema
t1: Open an existing schema in the Schema Editor and create a custom field group containing purchase preference attributes such as preferred category, price range, and brand affinity.
t2: Add the new custom field group to the schema and save it so that all datasets using that schema can capture and store purchase preference data.

title: CSV records into Profile dataset
t1: Upload a CSV file of customer records to an Experience Platform dataset that is mapped to an XDM schema.
t2: Enable the dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile so the ingested records are merged into unified customer profiles.

title: Batch upload CRM data to profiles
t1: Upload your daily CRM export file to a Profile-enabled dataset by creating a batch and posting the file via the Batch Ingestion API.
t2: Close and trigger the batch so Experience Platform processes the file and merges the CRM records into unified real-time customer profiles.

title: FTP loyalty data to Platform
t1: Connect the FTP source connector to your landing zone and ingest the weekly loyalty tier update files as a batch dataset in Experience Platform.
t2: Map the ingested batch data to your loyalty XDM schema so the tier updates are validated and loaded into the target dataset.

title: Ingest Parquet file into dataset
t1: Upload a Parquet file containing customer attribute updates to Experience Platform by creating a batch against an existing dataset.
t2: Complete and close the batch so Platform validates and ingests the Parquet records into the target dataset.

title: Stream mobile checkout events to Platform
t1: Authenticate and connect your mobile app to the Platform HTTP API streaming endpoint to begin sending real-time checkout events.
t2: Stream the checkout event payloads to the endpoint so they are ingested immediately into Platform datasets and Real-Time Customer Profile.

title: Stream retail POS events to Platform
t1: Configure a streaming HTTP API source connector to receive real-time point-of-sale transaction events from retail store systems.
t2: Validate that the streamed POS events are landing in the target dataset and appearing in customer profiles in real time.

title: Stream search events to Platform
t1: Instrument your website with the Web SDK to capture real-time search behavior events and send them to the Edge Network.
t2: Configure a datastream on the Edge Network to route the incoming search events into Experience Platform for immediate profile and dataset updates.

title: Collect web events via Edge Network
t1: Install and configure the AEP Web SDK on your website to capture page view and cart events as XDM-formatted data.
t2: Send the captured events through the Edge Network, which routes the data into Experience Platform for real-time profile ingestion.

title: Connect Analytics and map to XDM
t1: Connect an Adobe Analytics report suite as a source in Experience Platform to begin streaming its data into the platform.
t2: Map the report suite's dimensions and metrics to the corresponding XDM fields so the data conforms to the standard schema.

title: Audience Manager segments to datasets
source: Data Ingestion / Ingest from Audience Manager
t1: Connect Adobe Audience Manager as a source in Experience Platform to stream your segments and traits into the platform.
t2: Map the incoming Audience Manager segments and traits to an Experience Platform dataset so they are available for profile and segmentation use.

title: Marketo leads and activities to Platform
t1: Configure the Marketo source connector by authenticating with your Marketo instance and selecting the lead and activity datasets to sync.
t2: Run the dataflow so that Marketo lead and activity records stream continuously into your Platform datasets.

title: Schedule S3 transaction file ingestion
source: Data Ingestion / Ingest from cloud storage
t1: Connect your Amazon S3 bucket as a source and configure a dataflow that maps the daily transaction file fields to your target Platform dataset schema.
t2: Set a recurring ingestion schedule on the dataflow so Platform automatically pulls each new transaction file from S3 into the dataset on a daily basis.

title: Connect Salesforce and map to XDM
t1: Configure a Salesforce CRM source connector in Experience Platform by authenticating and selecting the contact object to ingest.
t2: Map the Salesforce contact fields to their corresponding XDM schema fields so the ingested data conforms to the unified data model.

title: Connect PostgreSQL and schedule ingestion
t1: Connect your PostgreSQL database as a source in Experience Platform by providing credentials and selecting the tables to ingest.
t2: Configure a scheduled dataflow to run nightly incremental ingestion, pulling only new or updated records into a Platform dataset.

title: Stream events via HTTP API inlet
source: Data Ingestion / Stream via HTTP API
t1: Create a streaming HTTP API inlet in Experience Platform to generate a unique endpoint URL for receiving real-time data.
t2: POST JSON event payloads to that endpoint so Experience Platform immediately updates matching real-time customer profiles with the new data.

title: Connect streaming source for real-time ingestion
t1: Configure a third-party streaming source connector in Experience Platform by providing authentication credentials and mapping incoming event fields to your target XDM schema.
t2: Activate the dataflow so that events streamed from the third-party source are continuously ingested into your Platform dataset in real time.

title: Monitor pipeline and fix failed batch
t1: Open the monitoring dashboard to inspect the ingestion pipeline and identify a batch job that has failed with errors.
t2: Diagnose the reported error details from the failed batch, correct the underlying data issue, and re-ingest the batch to complete the pipeline successfully.

title: Label identity fields in profile schema
t1: Open a profile schema in the Schema Editor and mark the email, phone, and CRM ID fields as identity fields by assigning each an identity namespace.
t2: Designate one identity field as the primary identity so Experience Platform can stitch data fragments into a unified real-time customer profile.

title: Set primary and secondary identity fields
t1: Open the loyalty program ID field in the schema editor and mark it as the primary identity, assigning it to the appropriate identity namespace.
t2: Open the email field in the same schema and mark it as a secondary identity so Experience Platform links both fields when building unified profiles.

title: Set ECID as primary identity
t1: Open the Experience Event schema in the Schema Editor and select the ECID field to configure its identity descriptor.
t2: Enable the identity toggle, choose the Identity namespace as ECID, and mark it as the primary identity for that schema.

title: Ingest data to build identity graph
t1: Ingest customer records containing multiple identity fields, such as email, phone, and CRM ID, into Experience Platform.
t2: Identity Service automatically links those identity fields to build a unified identity graph connecting all records to a single profile.

title: Stitch cross-channel identities into graph
t1: Ingest web, mobile, and CRM data into Experience Platform, each carrying identity namespaces such as ECID, email, and customer ID.
t2: Identity Service links those namespaces into a unified identity graph, stitching all cross-channel interactions into a single customer view.

title: Link anonymous visitor to known profile
t1: Capture the anonymous visitor's ECID from their website session and record their browsing behavior against that temporary identity.
t2: When the visitor logs in, Identity Service links their ECID to their known Customer ID, merging the anonymous activity into their unified real-time profile.

title: Merge device ID at app login
t1: Capture the mobile device ID collected during anonymous app browsing and link it to the customer's authenticated identity namespace at the moment of login.
t2: Identity Service merges the device ID into the existing customer profile, unifying all prior anonymous interactions with the known customer's profile in real time.

title: Link guest checkout to known profile
t1: Capture the email address submitted during guest checkout on the order confirmation page and send it to Identity Service as a new identity event.
t2: Identity Service matches the submitted email to an existing known profile, merging the anonymous visitor's activity into the unified customer profile via the identity graph.

title: Verify VIP customer cross-channel identities
t1: Search for a VIP customer in the Identity Service using a known identifier such as their email or loyalty ID.
t2: Inspect the customer's identity graph to confirm all cross-channel identities, including web, mobile, and CRM, are correctly linked.

title: Enable CRM dataset for unified profiles
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Bring data into profile
t1: Ingest your CRM records into a dataset built on a schema that has an identity field and a Profile-enabled class.
t2: Enable the dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile so each ingested CRM record is stitched into a unified customer profile via the identity graph.

title: Enable dataset for loyalty profile enrichment
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Bring data into profile
t1: Ingest loyalty transaction data into a dataset built on a profile-enabled schema in Experience Platform.
t2: Toggle the dataset's Real-Time Customer Profile switch on so loyalty transactions are merged into unified customer profiles.

title: Mobile events into real-time profile
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Bring data into profile
t1: Instrument your mobile app with the Mobile SDK to stream behavioral event data into Experience Platform datasets backed by a Profile-enabled schema.
t2: Once ingested, Experience Platform merges the mobile event data into unified real-time customer profiles via the identity graph, making them available for personalization.

title: Merge policy prioritizing CRM data
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Create merge policies
t1: Create a merge policy in the Platform UI and set the attribute merge to Dataset Precedence, placing your CRM dataset above third-party datasets in the priority order.
t2: Save and activate the merge policy so that unified profiles are built using CRM attribute values whenever conflicts arise with third-party data.

title: Dataset precedence merge policy for B2B
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Create merge policies
t1: Create a merge policy for the B2B account profile view and set the merge method to dataset precedence, ordering your trusted account datasets from highest to lowest priority.
t2: Save and activate the merge policy so that when profile fragments are stitched, attributes from higher-priority account datasets override those from lower-priority sources.

title: Configure last-write-wins merge policy
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Create merge policies
t1: Create a merge policy in the Real-Time Customer Profile settings, selecting timestamp-ordered last-write-wins as the attribute merge strategy.
t2: Assign the merge policy to your streaming-enabled dataset so that the most recently ingested attribute values always overwrite older ones in the unified profile.

title: Sum purchases with computed attribute
t1: Define a computed attribute using a sum aggregation on the purchase amount field, scoped to a 30-day lookback window.
t2: Enable the computed attribute so it automatically calculates and updates each customer's total purchase amount on their real-time profile.

title: Track app sessions with computed attribute
t1: Define a computed attribute in the Profile UI that counts the number of app session events occurring within the past 7 days.
t2: Enable and publish the computed attribute so it is continuously calculated and available on each customer's real-time profile for segmentation and personalization.

title: Compute recency score from purchase events
t1: Define a computed attribute rule that calculates a recency score by referencing the customer's most recent purchase event date from their real-time profile.
t2: Publish the computed attribute so it is continuously evaluated and appended to each customer's unified profile for use in segmentation and personalization.

title: Delete former customer profile data
t1: Identify the former customer's identity namespace and ID, then submit a profile delete job targeting their unified profile in the profile store.
t2: Confirm the delete job completes successfully, verifying the former customer's data has been fully removed from the Real-Time Customer Profile store.

title: Upsert email opt-out preference field
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Update profile attributes
t1: Send a Profile Upsert API request with the customer's identity and updated email opt-out preference field to write the new attribute value into their profile.
t2: Verify the updated email opt-out preference is reflected in the customer's unified real-time profile by retrieving it via the Profile Access API.

title: Revoke consent via profile API upsert
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Update profile attributes
t1: Make a streaming upsert API call to the Profile Store with the customer's updated consent revocation attributes, targeting their identity.
t2: Experience Platform immediately overwrites the stored consent fields on the unified profile, halting any downstream activations that depend on consent.

title: Explore union schema for segmentation
t1: Navigate to the Union Schema view in Real-Time Customer Profile to see all merged attributes contributed by every schema sharing the same class.
t2: Use the consolidated list of available attributes from the union schema to inform and build precise segment definitions in the Segment Builder.

title: Capture product viewers who didn't purchase
t1: In Segment Builder, define an audience of customers who have a product view event but no corresponding purchase event within the same time window.
t2: Save the audience to make it available for activation in re-engagement campaigns targeting those browsing customers.

title: Build high-value customer audience
t1: Open Segment Builder and define a rule filtering profiles where the lifetime spend attribute exceeds your chosen threshold value.
t2: Save and publish the segment to create a high-value customer audience ready for activation.

title: Segment email openers last 7 days
t1: In Segment Builder, add a rule filtering profiles where the email open event occurred within the last 7 days.
t2: Save and publish the segment to create an audience of customers who recently opened an email.

title: Build churn-risk audience from recency
t1: In Segment Builder, add a rule filtering profiles where the days-since-last-purchase attribute exceeds your churn-risk threshold, such as 90 days.
t2: Save and publish the segment to create a churn-risk audience ready for activation to re-engagement campaigns.

title: Target inactive loyalty members
t1: In Segment Builder, define an audience rule that matches loyalty program members whose last site visit attribute is more than 60 days ago.
t2: Save and publish the audience so it is available for activation in re-engagement campaigns targeting those lapsed loyalty members.

title: Score audience from propensity threshold
t1: Configure and run a Customer AI model to generate propensity scores for each customer profile.
t2: Build an audience in Segment Builder by filtering profiles whose Customer AI propensity score exceeds your defined threshold.

title: Combine purchase history for holiday audience
t1: Ingest both in-store and online purchase history data into Experience Platform and merge them into unified real-time customer profiles.
t2: Use Segment Builder to define a holiday campaign audience by combining rules that filter profiles based on in-store and online purchase activity.

title: B2B accounts with large open opportunities
t1: In Segment Builder, switch to account profiles and add a filter for open opportunities where deal size exceeds your defined revenue threshold.
t2: Save the segment to generate a B2B audience of high-value accounts ready for activation to sales or advertising destinations.

title: Real-time browsing to product segment
t1: Enable streaming segmentation on an audience rule that fires when a customer views a product page, qualifying them instantly as they browse.
t2: Use the continuously updated audience membership to trigger real-time personalization or journey actions for those customers.

title: Cart add triggers push notification audience
t1: Configure a streaming segment that qualifies customers in real time the moment they add an item to their cart.
t2: Trigger a push notification journey automatically when a customer qualifies for that audience.

title: Instant re-engagement on session exit
t1: Define a streaming segment rule that qualifies customers who completed a browsing session without making a purchase, so they are evaluated in real time as session-end events arrive.
t2: Activate the streaming audience to your re-engagement destination so matched customers receive a personalized follow-up message within seconds of their session ending.

title: Instant VIP qualification on spend threshold
t1: Define a streaming segment rule that qualifies customers the moment their cumulative spend crosses the VIP threshold, evaluated in real time as each purchase event arrives.
t2: Activate the VIP segment to your personalization and messaging destinations so customers receive VIP treatment instantly upon qualification.

title: On-demand batch evaluation for urgent campaign
t1: Create a new audience targeting customers likely to buy weather-related products and trigger an on-demand batch segmentation job to evaluate it immediately.
t2: Once the batch job completes and profiles are populated, activate the fully evaluated audience to your campaign destination without waiting for the next scheduled run.

title: On-demand evaluate audience for flash-sale
t1: Manually trigger an on-demand batch segmentation job for the target audience to force evaluation outside the scheduled window.
t2: Once the evaluation job completes and the audience membership is refreshed, activate the updated audience to your destination for the flash-sale campaign.

title: Connect and share audiences with partner
t1: Send a Segment Match connection request to your retail partner by entering their IMS organization ID and configuring the data sharing terms.
t2: Once the partner accepts the connection, select and share the approved audience segments with them through the established Segment Match feed.

title: Share buyer audience via Segment Match
t1: Create a high-intent buyer audience in Segment Builder and configure a Segment Match feed to share it with your media partner.
t2: Your media partner accepts the Segment Match feed and receives the overlapping audience for activation in their own Platform instance.

title: Receive partner segment for prospecting
t1: Accept the shared segment sent by your CPG partner through Segment Match to receive their audience into your sandbox.
t2: Activate the received partner audience to your advertising destination to run a prospecting campaign against it.

title: Authenticate and set up Facebook destination
t1: Authenticate to Facebook Custom Audiences by providing your Facebook account credentials and granting the required permissions in the destination configuration.
t2: Complete the destination setup by specifying the connection details, data export settings, and saving the configured Facebook Custom Audiences destination in Platform.

title: Connect Platform to Google Ads
t1: Configure and authenticate a new Google Ads destination in the Destinations catalog by providing your account credentials and connection settings.
t2: Activate your first-party audience to the connected Google Ads destination to enable targeted ad delivery.

title: Connect LinkedIn destination for B2B targeting
t1: Authenticate and configure a new LinkedIn Matched Audiences destination in the Destinations catalog by providing your LinkedIn account credentials and mapping settings.
t2: Activate your B2B account-based audience to the connected LinkedIn destination so matched accounts receive targeted ads.

title: Activate high-value audience to email
t1: Connect your email service provider as a destination in Experience Platform and configure the connection settings.
t2: Select the high-value customer audience and activate it to that email service provider destination for campaign delivery.

title: Activate churn-risk audience to CRM
t1: Connect your CRM platform as a destination in Experience Platform and configure the authentication and mapping settings.
t2: Activate your churn-risk audience to that connected CRM destination so sales and retention teams can launch targeted outreach.

title: Activate cart abandoners to display ads
t1: Connect a programmatic display advertising destination in Experience Platform and configure the connection credentials and mapping settings.
t2: Activate the cart abandonment audience to that connected destination so ads are served to those shoppers across the display network.

title: Export raw events dataset to Azure
t1: Connect your Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 account as a destination in Experience Platform.
t2: Select the raw events dataset and activate it to that Azure Data Lake destination for downstream analysis.

title: Schedule nightly profile data export
t1: Connect a cloud storage destination and select the dataset containing profile attribute data to export.
t2: Configure a nightly export schedule so the dataset is automatically delivered to the cloud storage bucket each night.

title: Connect Azure Blob for audience exports
t1: Configure the Azure Blob Storage destination by providing your storage account credentials, container name, and scheduled export settings.
t2: Activate the desired audience to the configured Azure Blob destination so membership data is exported on the defined schedule.

title: Sync B2B audience to Marketo
t1: Build a high-intent B2B audience in Real-Time CDP by segmenting profiles based on product interest signals and account attributes.
t2: Connect the Marketo Engage destination and activate that audience so matched leads are automatically enrolled in Marketo nurturing sequences.

title: Upload email audience to Google
t1: Connect the Google Customer Match destination and map your first-party email identity fields to the required Google attributes.
t2: Activate your email audience to the configured Google Customer Match destination so Google can match profiles for search retargeting.

title: Seed audience to Facebook lookalike
t1: Build a seed audience of your highest-value customers in Real-Time CDP to use as the lookalike source for Facebook Ads prospecting.
t2: Connect the Facebook Custom Audiences destination and activate the seed audience so Facebook can generate a lookalike audience to reach new prospective customers.

title: Activate audience via LiveRamp destination
t1: Connect the LiveRamp destination and activate your first-party audience by mapping identity fields such as email or phone to LiveRamp's RampID.
t2: LiveRamp distributes the resolved RampIDs to connected TV and addressable media partners, enabling privacy-safe audience targeting across those channels.

title: Share audience to Snowflake data science
t1: Connect a Snowflake batch data share destination and activate the target Platform audience to it.
t2: The data science team queries the shared Snowflake dataset to access the audience profiles for their analysis.

title: Activate high-value segment to Target
t1: Build a high-value customer audience in Real-Time CDP and connect Adobe Target as an activation destination.
t2: Activate the audience to Adobe Target so it can personalize homepage content in real time for those customers.

title: Profile attributes to Target personalization
t1: Connect Adobe Target as a destination and activate a Real-Time CDP audience with profile attributes, such as product preferences and purchase history, to Target.
t2: Use those streamed profile attributes inside Target to deliver personalized product recommendations to each visitor in real time.

title: Train model and segment churners
t1: Configure and train a Customer AI churn propensity model by selecting the dataset, defining the churn event, and running the model to generate propensity scores for each customer profile.
t2: Build an audience segment filtered to customers with high churn propensity scores and activate it to a campaign destination to deliver a personalized win-back offer.

title: Configure Customer AI and activate audience
t1: Configure a Customer AI model with purchase propensity as the goal, select the input dataset, and run the model to generate propensity scores for each profile.
t2: Build an audience by filtering profiles above the high-intent score threshold and activate that audience to your advertising or email destination.

title: Score profiles and target upsell audience
t1: Configure and run a Customer AI model to generate upsell propensity scores for each customer profile.
t2: Build an audience segment using the propensity score threshold and activate it to your campaign destination.

title: Churn model scores to retention journey
t1: Configure and run a Customer AI churn prediction model to generate propensity-to-churn scores for each customer profile.
t2: Build an audience of high-churn-risk customers using those propensity scores and activate them into a don't-lose retention journey.

title: Score and retarget app uninstall risk
t1: Configure a Customer AI model using behavioral data to predict which users are at risk of uninstalling the app.
t2: Run the model to generate propensity scores and build an audience of high-risk users from those scores.
t3: Activate the at-risk audience to your mobile and advertising destinations to deliver targeted re-engagement campaigns.

title: Measure channel ROI with Attribution AI
t1: Configure an Attribution AI instance by defining conversion events and mapping marketing touchpoints across channels.
t2: Run the Attribution AI model to generate attribution scores for each touchpoint in the customer journey.
t3: Analyze the attribution results to measure each channel's contribution to conversions and calculate ROI.

title: Attribution AI to budget reallocation
t1: Configure and run an Attribution AI model instance, selecting the conversion events and marketing touchpoints to analyze.
t2: Review the generated attribution scores and channel performance insights to see which channels drive the most conversions.
t3: Reallocate your marketing budget toward the highest-performing channels identified by the Attribution AI results.

title: Attribution AI scores to CJA dashboard
t1: Configure an Attribution AI instance by selecting your conversion events, touchpoint channels, and attribution model to generate multi-touch credit scores.
t2: Run the Attribution AI model to produce channel-level attribution scores and surface the results as a dataset in Experience Platform.
t3: Connect the Attribution AI scores dataset to Customer Journey Analytics and build an executive dashboard visualizing channel contribution and conversion impact.

title: Query visitor counts by marketing channel
t1: Connect to Query Service and write a SQL query targeting the Platform dataset that contains your web analytics and marketing channel data.
t2: Execute the query to aggregate and calculate unique visitor counts grouped by each marketing channel.
t3: Review the returned results to compare visitor volumes across channels and export the data for reporting.

title: Validate ingested batch data quality
t1: Ingest a batch of customer data into an Experience Platform dataset.
t2: Run a SQL query in Query Service against the ingested dataset to check field values, null counts, and record totals.
t3: Review the query results to confirm data quality and flag any records that fail validation rules.

title: Derive high-value customer dataset
t1: Connect to Query Service and write a SQL query that aggregates behavioral event data to calculate each customer's total spend and purchase frequency.
t2: Run a CTAS query to materialize the aggregated results as a new derived dataset stored in Experience Platform.
t3: Enable the derived dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile so high-value customer attributes are available for segmentation and activation.

title: Query Service data to Tableau visualization
t1: Connect Tableau to Query Service using the PostgreSQL credentials provided in the Experience Platform UI.
t2: Write a SQL query in Tableau to pull audience membership and performance metrics from the platform datasets.
t3: Build an interactive visualization in Tableau dashboarding the audience performance results from the query.

title: Query inactive customers via SQL
t1: Open Query Service and write a SQL query that filters customer profiles with no purchase events in the last 30 days.
t2: Run the query against your Experience Platform datasets to retrieve the list of inactive customers.
t3: Save the query results as a new dataset to build an audience for re-engagement campaigns.

title: Event history to churn feature dataset
t1: Write a SQL query in Query Service that analyzes event history to calculate churn-indicator features such as days since last activity and session frequency.
t2: Execute the SQL query to materialize the results as a new derived dataset stored in Experience Platform.
t3: Use the derived churn-indicator dataset to build segments or feed AI models for churn prediction.

title: Validate streaming events against XDM schema
t1: Ingest streaming events into Experience Platform so they land in a dataset backed by your target XDM schema.
t2: Run a Query Service SQL query against the dataset to inspect field values, types, and structure of the ingested events.
t3: Compare the query results against the expected XDM schema fields to confirm all events conform and flag any mismatches.

title: Label third-party data fields for compliance
t1: Open the schema containing contractually restricted third-party data fields in the Schema Editor.
t2: Select each restricted field and apply the appropriate DULE data usage labels to mark them as third-party contractual data.
t3: Save the labeled schema so downstream governance policies can enforce restrictions on those fields.

title: Label PII fields in profile schema
t1: Open an existing profile schema in the Schema Editor and identify the fields that contain personally identifiable information.
t2: Apply the appropriate sensitive personal data usage labels to each PII field to mark them as restricted.
t3: Save the labeled schema so that downstream data governance policies can enforce restrictions on those fields.

title: Label device ID fields restrict stitching
t1: Open the event schema in the Schema Editor and navigate to the device ID fields that should not be used for identity stitching.
t2: Apply the appropriate data usage labels, such as I2 or device-linkage restriction labels, directly to those device ID fields.
t3: Create a data governance policy that enforces those labels to block identity stitching operations on the labeled device ID fields.

title: Block labeled fields from ad networks
t1: Apply restrictive data usage labels to the schema fields that contain sensitive customer data.
t2: Navigate to Data Governance policies and create a new policy that references those applied labels.
t3: Define the policy rule to block activation of those labeled fields to advertising network destinations.

title: Block health data from social media
t1: Apply sensitive health data usage labels to the schema fields that contain patient or medical information.
t2: Create a data usage policy that restricts any data labeled as health information from being activated to social media destinations.
t3: Enforce the policy so that any activation attempt to a social media destination containing health-labeled data is automatically blocked.

title: Policy blocks restricted audience activation
t1: Apply a restrictive data usage label to a schema field containing sensitive customer data.
t2: Create a data usage policy that prohibits activating data with that label to advertising destinations.
t3: Attempt to activate an audience containing that labeled data and verify the platform automatically blocks it.

title: Label, policy, and enforce at destination
t1: Apply data usage labels to sensitive schema fields to classify the data as restricted for advertising use.
t2: Create a data usage policy that blocks activation of those labeled fields to advertising destinations.
t3: Attempt to activate the audience to an ad destination and confirm the policy violation is enforced and blocked.

title: Healthcare data governance end-to-end
t1: Apply HIPAA-aligned data usage labels to sensitive health-related schema fields to mark them as restricted for marketing use.
t2: Create data usage policies that block those labeled fields from being activated to advertising or third-party marketing destinations.
t3: Activate a compliant patient audience to an approved destination, letting Platform enforce the policies and block any violations automatically.

title: Submit and fulfill GDPR access request
t1: Submit a GDPR data access job via the Privacy Service API or UI, specifying the customer's identity and regulation type.
t2: Privacy Service locates and compiles all stored data associated with that customer identity across Experience Platform datasets.
t3: Download the exported data package from the completed job and deliver it to the customer to fulfill the access request.

title: Fulfill CCPA customer data deletion
t1: Submit a CCPA deletion request to Privacy Service by providing the customer's identity details and namespace.
t2: Privacy Service propagates the deletion job to all connected Platform services that hold the customer's data.
t3: Confirm the deletion is complete by reviewing the job status once all services report successful erasure.

title: Collect and forward opt-out signals
t1: Install the AEP Privacy JavaScript library on your website to capture visitor opt-out signals.
t2: Configure the library to detect and collect opt-out preferences submitted by site visitors.
t3: Forward the collected opt-out signals to Adobe Privacy Service for processing and compliance enforcement.

title: Automate privacy requests via API
t1: Authenticate with the Privacy Service REST API and construct a JSON payload containing the data subject identities and the type of privacy request to submit.
t2: POST the payload to the Privacy Service API endpoint to programmatically create delete or access jobs at scale for all relevant Experience Cloud products.
t3: Poll the API for job status updates and retrieve the completed results to confirm each privacy request has been fulfilled.

title: Monitor deletion requests via event subscription
t1: Register a webhook or event listener by subscribing to Privacy Service events in the Adobe Developer Console.
t2: Submit a privacy deletion request through the Privacy Service API to trigger a job.
t3: Receive a real-time event notification when the deletion job completes and log the result for compliance tracking.

title: Subscribe to segment job failure alert
t1: Navigate to the Alerts section in Experience Platform and browse the available alert types.
t2: Select the segment job failure alert and subscribe to it with your email or notification preference.
t3: Receive an immediate notification when an audience evaluation job fails so you can investigate and resolve the issue.

title: Monitor pipeline with ingestion delay alert
t1: Navigate to Alerts in Experience Platform and browse the available alert rules to find the ingestion delay metric alert.
t2: Enable the ingestion delay alert and configure its threshold and notification recipients to match your critical daily pipeline's requirements.
t3: Receive an alert notification when the pipeline's ingestion delay exceeds the defined threshold, allowing you to investigate and resolve the issue promptly.

title: Alert for destination activation failure
t1: Navigate to the destination connection for your high-priority campaign audience and open the alerts configuration panel.
t2: Subscribe to the destination activation failure alert and specify the notification recipients for your team.
t3: Trigger a test activation to confirm the alert fires correctly when a failure occurs.

title: Monitor batch ingestion job success
t1: Run a batch ingestion job to load data from your source into an Experience Platform dataset.
t2: Open the Monitoring dashboard in the platform UI to locate the completed batch ingestion run.
t3: Review the batch status, record counts, and any error details to confirm the ingestion succeeded.

title: Monitor audience activation dataflow status
t1: Publish a new audience and activate it to an advertising destination in the Destinations workspace.
t2: Navigate to the Monitoring dashboard and open the Segment Activation view to locate the dataflow run.
t3: Inspect the dataflow run details to confirm successful delivery or diagnose any activation errors.

title: Diagnose missing records in source dataflow
t1: Navigate to the Monitoring dashboard and select the source connector to view its dataflow run history.
t2: Open a failed or partial run to inspect the error details, identifying which records were skipped or rejected.
t3: Use the error diagnostics and record counts to pinpoint the root cause and correct the source data or mapping configuration.

title: Enable AI Assistant for team member
t1: Open Admin Console and confirm the team member has been added as a user in your AEP product profile.
t2: Navigate to Permissions UI and open the role assigned to that team member.
t3: Add the AI Assistant permission to the role so the team member can access AI Assistant features.

title: Learn merge policies with AI Assistant
t1: Ask AI Assistant to explain what merge policies are and how they control which data fragments are combined in a unified profile.
t2: Ask AI Assistant how different merge policy settings, such as timestamp-ordered or custom priority, affect which attribute values appear during a profile lookup.
t3: Use the knowledge gained to review and configure your merge policies so profile lookups return the correct and most relevant customer data.

title: Ask AI for destination activation guide
t1: Open AI Assistant in Experience Platform and ask for a step-by-step guide on activating an audience to a new destination.
t2: AI Assistant returns a structured walkthrough covering how to connect the destination and configure the activation settings.
t3: Follow the returned steps to connect your destination and activate your audience successfully.

title: Troubleshoot streaming segment evaluation failure
t1: Ask AI Assistant why your streaming segment is not evaluating in real time, describing the segment conditions and data sources involved.
t2: Review AI Assistant's explanation of common causes, such as unsupported segment operators, missing profile merge policies, or edge cases that prevent streaming evaluation.
t3: Apply the recommended fix, such as updating the segment rule to use streaming-compatible operators, and confirm real-time evaluation resumes.

title: Find empty audiences with AI Assistant
t1: Open AI Assistant in your sandbox and ask how many audiences currently have zero profiles.
t2: AI Assistant queries the operational metadata and returns a list of audiences with zero profile counts.
t3: Review the returned audience list to identify and clean up or troubleshoot the empty audiences.

title: Find journeys using a specific audience
t1: Open AI Assistant in Journey Optimizer and ask which journeys are currently using a specific named audience.
t2: AI Assistant queries the operational metadata and returns a list of live journeys referencing that audience.
t3: Review the returned journey list to understand the audience's active usage across all running journeys.

title: Find and delete unused audiences
t1: Ask AI Assistant to list all audiences that have never been activated to any destination.
t2: Review the returned list of inactive audiences and confirm which ones are safe to remove.
t3: Delete the unused audiences to keep your audience inventory clean and manageable.

title: Find and remove empty audiences pre-migration
t1: Ask AI Assistant to list all audiences with zero profiles currently defined in your sandbox.
t2: Review the returned list and delete the empty audiences to clean up the sandbox.
t3: Proceed with the sandbox migration knowing no unused audiences will be carried over.

title: Check dependencies before deleting attribute
t1: Ask AI Assistant which datasets, segments, and journeys depend on a specific schema attribute you plan to delete.
t2: Review the list of dependent objects returned by AI Assistant to understand the full impact of the deletion.
t3: Remove or update all dependent objects, then safely delete the schema attribute.

title: Schema field change impact analysis
t1: Identify the schema field you plan to modify and ask AI Assistant to trace its lineage across datasets, segments, and journeys.
t2: Review the downstream dependencies surfaced by AI Assistant to understand which audiences, attributes, and journeys rely on that field.
t3: Use the impact analysis results to update or remap all affected downstream assets before applying the schema field change.

title: Partner data to prospecting audience
t1: Ingest partner-provided prospect data into Experience Platform and map it to a partner ID namespace.
t2: Build a prospecting audience in Segment Builder using partner attributes to target net-new customers who have never interacted with your brand.
t3: Activate the prospecting audience to a paid media destination to reach those new customers offsite.

title: Enrich profiles with partner financial attributes
t1: Ingest partner-provided financial segment attributes into Experience Platform using a partner data source connection.
t2: Map and merge those partner attributes onto existing known customer profiles using identity resolution.
t3: Use the enriched profiles to build audiences segmented by financial attributes for targeted activation.

title: Personalize content for anonymous visitors
source: Partner Data / Personalize for unknown visitors
t1: Capture anonymous website visitor signals and enrich them with partner-provided identity attributes to build a temporary profile.
t2: Match the enriched anonymous profile to a relevant audience segment using partner identity resolution.
t3: Deliver personalized website content to the anonymous visitor based on their matched audience segment.

title: Partner data to prospecting audience
t1: Ingest partner-provided enrichment data to identify prospect profiles that resemble your best existing customers.
t2: Build a lookalike prospecting audience in Segment Builder using the partner attributes and similarity signals.
t3: Activate the prospecting audience to offsite advertising destinations to acquire new customers.

title: Discover and deploy cart re-engagement playbook
source: Use Case Playbooks / Browse and instantiate
t1: Browse the Use Case Playbook gallery and select the abandoned cart re-engagement playbook that matches your goal.
t2: Create an instance of the playbook to automatically generate its supporting schemas, audiences, and journey assets.
t3: Review and publish the generated assets to your sandbox so the re-engagement journey is ready to activate.

title: Churn prevention playbook to instance
source: Use Case Playbooks / Browse and instantiate
t1: Browse the Use Case Playbooks gallery and select a churn prevention playbook that matches your business goal.
t2: Create an instance of the selected playbook inside your inspiration sandbox.
t3: Review the generated assets, such as journeys and audiences, that the playbook instance produces.

title: B2B Account Nurture Playbook to ABM
source: Use Case Playbooks / Browse and instantiate
t1: Browse the Use Case Playbook gallery and select a B2B account nurture playbook that matches your ABM campaign goals.
t2: Create an instance of the playbook to generate its associated assets, including audiences, journeys, and schemas.
t3: Publish the generated playbook assets to your sandbox and use them as the foundation for your new ABM campaign.

title: Review and import playbook artifacts
t1: Browse the generated playbook artifacts, such as schemas, segments, and journeys, and review them for accuracy.
t2: Publish the playbook instance to make its assets available for export.
t3: Import the published playbook package into your development sandbox to begin working with the assets.

title: Set up playbook inspiration sandbox
t1: Create a dedicated sandbox in Experience Platform to serve as your playbook inspiration environment.
t2: Add the required users to the sandbox in Admin Console and assign the necessary playbook permissions in the Permissions UI.
t3: Navigate to Use Case Playbooks in the configured sandbox to browse and instantiate playbook templates.

title: Build KPI dashboard for audience metrics
t1: Create a custom dashboard in Experience Platform and add widgets to visualize audience sizes and profile counts.
t2: Configure each widget with the relevant attributes and metrics, including activation counts and segment membership data.
t3: Save and publish the dashboard so stakeholders can monitor real-time KPI trends across audiences and destinations.

title: Build executive segment and delivery dashboard
t1: Create a custom dashboard and add widgets displaying segment population sizes, growth trends, and qualification rates.
t2: Add destination delivery widgets to the dashboard to surface activation success rates and audience export volumes per destination.
t3: Save and share the completed dashboard with executives for a unified view of segment health and delivery performance.

title: Build ingestion health tracking dashboard
t1: Create a custom dashboard in the Dashboards UI and configure it to monitor batch ingestion data.
t2: Add widgets that display daily batch job metrics such as records ingested, failures, and success rates.
t3: Review the populated dashboard to track daily batch job success rates and identify ingestion issues.

title: Confirm and delete expired test dataset
t1: Review the test dataset in the data lake to confirm it is expired and no longer referenced by any active profiles or segments.
t2: Submit a dataset delete request through Data Hygiene to schedule the dataset for removal from the data lake.
t3: Verify the deletion has completed by confirming the dataset no longer appears in the catalog.

title: Find and delete a failed batch
t1: Monitor batch ingestion logs to identify a failed or incorrect batch that introduced bad records into the platform.
t2: Submit a batch delete request targeting that specific batch ID to remove its records from all datasets.
t3: Verify the deletion by confirming the incorrect records no longer appear in customer profiles or query results.

title: Set expiration on campaign dataset
t1: Navigate to the dataset in Experience Platform and open the Data Hygiene settings for that dataset.
t2: Configure an automatic expiration date by specifying the future date on which the temporary campaign dataset should be deleted.
t3: Save the expiration schedule so the platform automatically removes the dataset and its data on the configured date.

title: Expire inactive pseudonymous profiles automatically
t1: Identify pseudonymous profiles in your dataset that lack a known identity and have been inactive for 30 days.
t2: Configure a pseudonymous profile expiration policy in Data Hygiene, setting the TTL threshold to 30 days of inactivity.
t3: Platform automatically deletes profiles matching the expiration criteria, keeping your profile store clean and compliant.

title: Query stale records before deletion
t1: Run Query Service SQL queries to identify records that have not been updated or interacted with beyond a defined staleness threshold.
t2: Review and validate the query results to confirm which records are eligible for deletion and export the list of affected identities.
t3: Submit a data hygiene delete job targeting those confirmed stale identities to remove them from the platform.

title: Size audience and resolve journey conflicts
source: Marketing Workflows / Plan and size campaign
t1: Use Segment Builder to define your campaign audience and review the estimated profile count to confirm sufficient reach.
t2: Check active journeys in Journey Optimizer to identify any audience overlaps or conflicting messages targeting the same profiles.
t3: Resolve conflicts by adjusting audience criteria or suppressing overlapping profiles, then approve the campaign for launch.

title: Configure and publish re-engagement journey
t1: Build a re-engagement audience in Journey Optimizer by identifying customers who have not interacted recently.
t2: Configure the journey canvas with entry conditions, wait steps, and personalized re-engagement messages across email and SMS channels.
t3: Review the journey settings and publish it so customers enter and receive re-engagement communications automatically.

title: Review post-campaign conversion performance
t1: Connect your campaign data source to Customer Journey Analytics and create a connection with the relevant datasets.
t2: Build a data view in Customer Journey Analytics that defines the conversion metrics and dimensions you want to analyze.
t3: Open a workspace project, add a funnel and conversion rate visualization, and review post-campaign performance across channels.

title: AI scores drive win-back offer
t1: Run a Customer AI propensity model to score customers by their likelihood to churn.
t2: Build an audience of high-churn-risk customers by filtering profiles on those AI-generated scores.
t3: Trigger a personalized win-back journey that delivers a tailored retention offer across email and mobile.

title: Trigger cart abandonment push notification
t1: Detect when a customer adds items to their cart but does not complete checkout within a defined time window.
t2: Enroll the customer in a Journey Optimizer journey triggered by the cart abandonment event.
t3: Send a personalized push notification reminding the customer of their abandoned cart items.

title: Notify customers of loyalty tier upgrade
t1: Build an audience of customers who have newly qualified for a higher loyalty tier based on their recent activity and spend.
t2: Design a journey in Journey Optimizer that triggers when a customer enters that audience and delivers a personalized tier upgrade notification.
t3: Publish the journey so newly qualified customers automatically receive their tier upgrade notification across their preferred channel.

title: Review channel attribution after product launch
t1: Open Customer Journey Analytics and navigate to the product launch campaign workspace created before go-live.
t2: Apply a date range covering the launch period to filter all panels and visualizations to the relevant timeframe.
t3: Review the channel attribution KPIs across touchpoints to identify which channels drove the most conversions.

title: Query audience size and check conflicts
t1: Ask the Adobe Marketing Agent to query the size of your target audience and return the current profile count.
t2: Prompt the agent to scan all live journeys and identify any that already target the same audience.
t3: Review the agent's conflict report and adjust your journey or audience before proceeding with activation.

title: Connect to media partner via Segment Match
t1: Enter your media partner's IMS Organization ID in Segment Match to initiate a connection request.
t2: Wait for the partner organization to review and accept the incoming connection request on their end.
t3: Confirm the active connection in Segment Match so you can begin sharing audience segments with that partner.

title: Label audience before Segment Match share
t1: Apply data usage labels to the schema fields underlying your audience to mark data as restricted for sharing.
t2: Create a data usage policy that enforces those labels and governs how the audience data may be exported.
t3: Share the governed audience with a partner via Segment Match, ensuring policy controls are enforced before data leaves.

title: Share retail buyer audience with partner
t1: Build a high-intent retail buyer audience in Segment Builder using purchase behavior and engagement signals.
t2: Create a Segment Match feed and invite your co-marketing partner organization to receive the shared audience.
t3: Partner accepts the feed and activates the shared audience in their own Platform sandbox for co-marketing campaigns.

title: Receive and activate partner audience
t1: Accept the segment shared by your partner through Segment Match to receive the audience into your sandbox.
t2: Review and validate the received audience profiles to confirm they meet your prospecting campaign criteria.
t3: Activate the partner-shared audience to your advertising destination to launch the prospecting campaign.

title: Preview audience overlap before partner share
t1: Select the audience segment you want to evaluate and choose a potential data-sharing partner in Segment Match.
t2: Run the pre-share overlap estimation to see how many profiles your audience shares with the partner's audience.
t3: Review the estimated overlap insights and decide whether the overlap justifies proceeding with the data share.

title: Collect, unify, segment, and activate
t1: Ingest customer data from all your sources into Experience Platform to build a complete data foundation.
t2: Stitch the ingested data into unified real-time customer profiles using the identity graph.
t3: Build audiences from those profiles and activate them to your marketing destinations.

title: Re-engage checkout abandoners intelligently
t1: Identify customers who started but did not complete the checkout flow using real-time behavioral data.
t2: Build a re-engagement audience from those customers and predict the best time and channel to reach them.
t3: Deliver a personalized re-engagement message through the optimal channel to bring them back to complete their purchase.

title: AI-powered churn prevention campaign
t1: Use Customer AI to score every customer profile with a churn propensity score based on their behavior.
t2: Build an audience of high-risk customers by filtering profiles above the churn score threshold.
t3: Activate the at-risk audience in real time to your email and advertising destinations with a retention offer.

title: Edge events to activated profile
t1: Stream customer events through the Edge Network using the Web SDK to capture real-time behavioral data.
t2: Experience Platform merges those events into a unified real-time customer profile using the identity graph.
t3: Activate the updated profile audience to a destination for immediate personalized engagement.

title: Collect, unify, and activate customer data
t1: Collect customer data from all channels and ingest it into Real-Time CDP.
t2: Unify the ingested data into a single real-time customer profile using the identity graph.
t3: Activate the unified profiles as audiences to your marketing and advertising destinations.

title: Plan, implement, and operate AEP
t1: Plan the AEP project by defining business goals, identifying data sources, and aligning stakeholders on requirements.
t2: Implement the solution by configuring schemas, ingesting data, and building audiences and journeys.
t3: Operate the platform by monitoring performance, refining audiences, and continuously optimizing outcomes.

title: Real-time profile to relevant offer
t1: Read the known customer's real-time profile attributes, including recent behavior and preferences.
t2: Use Next Best Offer decisioning to select the most contextually relevant offer for that customer.
t3: Deliver the personalized offer to the customer in the moment across their active channel.

title: CRM data to email segment
t1: Batch-ingest CRM customer records into Experience Platform using a source connector.
t2: The identity graph stitches ingested records into unified real-time customer profiles.
t3: Build an email audience segment from those unified profiles for campaign activation.

title: Analyze omnichannel conversion funnels
t1: Connect your online and offline data sources to Customer Journey Analytics by creating a connection to the relevant Platform datasets.
t2: Build a Data View to define the metrics and dimensions needed to represent each stage of your conversion funnel.
t3: Create a Fallout visualization in Analysis Workspace to identify where customers drop off across channels and optimize the journey.

title: Score, segment, and activate journeys
t1: Run Customer AI to generate propensity scores for each customer profile based on their behavior.
t2: Build a targeted audience segment by filtering profiles that meet your desired score threshold.
t3: Activate the audience in Journey Optimizer to deliver a personalized experience across channels.

title: Label audience data for consent compliance
t1: Identify the schema fields that contain customer consent and opt-out preferences and apply the appropriate data usage labels to them.
t2: Create a data usage policy that restricts activation of any data labeled with those consent-related labels.
t3: Attempt to activate the audience and let the policy enforcement automatically block or warn when opt-out preferences are violated.

title: Block behavioral data export to partners
t1: Apply data usage labels to behavioral data schema fields to mark them as restricted for third-party sharing.
t2: Create a data usage policy that references those labels and prohibits export to third-party partner destinations.
t3: Enable the policy so Platform enforces it and blocks any activation of labeled behavioral data to partner destinations.

title: Label, policy, and enforce financial data
t1: Apply sensitive financial data usage labels to the relevant schema fields to mark them as restricted.
t2: Create a data usage policy that blocks activation of those labeled fields to any advertising or external destination.
t3: Attempt to activate a segment containing those fields to a destination and confirm the policy enforcement blocks the action.

title: Label device IDs before partner sharing
t1: Navigate to the schema containing device ID fields and apply identity-stitching restriction labels to mark them as sensitive.
t2: Create a data usage policy that blocks any dataset carrying those labels from being activated to partner destinations.
t3: Attempt to activate the audience to a partner destination and confirm the policy enforcement blocks the restricted device ID fields.

title: Namespace setup for loyalty schema
t1: Create custom identity namespaces for each brand's loyalty program identifiers in the Identity Service namespace configuration.
t2: Apply those custom namespaces as identity descriptors to the relevant fields in the multi-brand loyalty program schema.
t3: Ingest loyalty records so the identity graph stitches each brand's member IDs into unified customer profiles.

title: Stitch in-store purchases to online profile
t1: Ingest offline in-store purchase records into Experience Platform, including the customer's email address as an identity field.
t2: Identity Service recognizes the shared email address and links the offline purchase records to the existing online profile in the identity graph.
t3: The unified profile now reflects both online behavior and in-store purchase history for complete cross-channel personalization.

title: Anonymous visitor to known profile
t1: Capture anonymous browsing behavior using a cookie-based ECID as the visitor browses your website before logging in.
t2: When the customer authenticates, link their known Customer ID to the existing ECID in the Identity Graph.
t3: Experience Platform merges the anonymous browsing history into the customer's unified real-time profile, enriching it with pre-login behavior.

title: Audit customer identity graph linkage
t1: Look up the customer's profile in Identity Service using a known identifier such as their email address.
t2: Open the identity graph viewer to see all linked identities associated with that customer's profile.
t3: Confirm that the customer's mobile device ID and web ECID are both present and connected in the graph.

title: Stream events into real-time profiles
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Bring data into profile
t1: Connect a streaming source and configure a dataset with an XDM ExperienceEvent schema to capture live customer events.
t2: Enable the dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile so that every incoming event immediately updates the relevant profile.
t3: Verify that streaming events are continuously merging into unified customer profiles using the profile viewer.

title: Compute average order value attribute
t1: Create a computed attribute definition that calculates average order value using a sum aggregation over a 90-day lookback window.
t2: Enable and publish the computed attribute so Platform begins processing historical and streaming order events into each customer's profile.
t3: Use the populated average order value attribute to build segments and personalize experiences for high-value customers.

title: Bulk delete test profiles before production
t1: Submit a bulk delete job targeting test account identities to remove their profiles from the profile store.
t2: Monitor the delete job status until it completes and all targeted profiles are confirmed as removed.
t3: Verify the profile store contains no residual test account data before promoting the environment to production.

title: Verify identity fields across union schema
t1: Open the union schema for your XDM class to see every dataset contributing fields to the merged profile view.
t2: Inspect the identity field columns across all contributing datasets to confirm each one includes the required identity descriptors.
t3: Flag any dataset missing a required identity field and update its schema to include the correct identity descriptor before re-ingesting.

title: SQL aggregation to lifetime value
t1: Connect to Query Service and write a SQL query that aggregates purchase event data from Platform datasets to compute total spend per customer.
t2: Run the query to generate a results table containing each customer's calculated lifetime value score.
t3: Save the query results as a new Platform dataset to use for segmentation and downstream activation.

title: Event history to product affinity dataset
t1: Connect to Query Service and explore the raw event history dataset to understand the structure of product interaction records.
t2: Write a CTAS query that aggregates product interaction events per customer to compute affinity scores and materializes the results as a new derived dataset.
t3: Use the newly created product-affinity feature dataset as an enrichment source for segmentation or AI model training.

title: Validate field mapping after migration
t1: Ingest migrated data into a new dataset backed by the updated target schema.
t2: Run a SQL query in Query Service to compare source field values against mapped fields in the new schema.
t3: Review the query results to confirm all field mappings are accurate and flag any discrepancies for correction.

title: Connect Tableau and report attribution
t1: Export your Query Service credentials from the Experience Platform UI to authenticate an external BI tool.
t2: Use those credentials to connect Tableau Desktop to the Query Service PostgreSQL endpoint.
t3: Build an attribution performance report in Tableau by querying your dataset directly through the live connection.

title: Diagnose batch ingestion failure monitoring
t1: Open the Monitoring dashboard and navigate to the Data Ingestion section to view recent batch runs.
t2: Identify the failed batch by its error status and click into it to inspect the run details.
t3: Review the error message and failed record details to diagnose the root cause of the ingestion failure.

title: Verify audience export counts at destination
t1: Activate an audience to a destination and trigger an export job to send profile data downstream.
t2: Navigate to the destination monitoring view to observe the export job status and profile counts.
t3: Compare the exported profile counts against expected audience size to confirm the activation completed successfully.

title: Subscribe and acknowledge destination alert
t1: Navigate to a destination dataflow in the platform and subscribe to the dataflow failure alert to enable notifications.
t2: Wait for the alert to trigger when the destination dataflow fails, then open the Alerts panel to view the notification.
t3: Acknowledge the triggered alert notification to mark it as reviewed and clear it from your active alerts list.

title: Find and fix recurring ingestion error
t1: Open the Sources monitoring dashboard and review the dataflow run history to identify a recurring schema validation error.
t2: Inspect the failed dataflow run details to pinpoint which schema field is causing the ingestion failure.
t3: Correct the schema mapping in the source connector configuration and re-run the dataflow to confirm successful ingestion.

title: Bulk CRM customer erasure job
t1: Export the list of customer identities requiring erasure from your CRM and format them into a Privacy Service API-compliant JSON payload.
t2: Submit the formatted payload as a bulk delete job to Privacy Service, which fans out erasure requests across all connected AEP data stores.
t3: Monitor the job status in Privacy Service UI until all deletions are confirmed complete and download the compliance report.

title: Submit and fulfill customer DSAR
