t1: Submit a data access request job for the customer through the Privacy Service API or UI, specifying their identity details.
t2: Privacy Service locates and compiles all personal data held for that customer across connected Experience Platform products.
t3: Download the completed data export report from Privacy Service and deliver it to the customer to fulfill the DSAR.

title: Webhook for privacy job status events
t1: Register a webhook endpoint in Adobe I/O Events to receive Privacy Service job status notifications.
t2: Subscribe to the relevant privacy job status events so that updates are routed to your registered webhook.
t3: Trigger your automated workflow logic when the webhook receives a privacy job status event payload.

title: Loyalty re-engagement playbook to journey
source: Use Case Playbooks / Browse and instantiate
t1: Browse the Use Case Playbook gallery and select a loyalty re-engagement playbook that matches your campaign goal.
t2: Create an instance of the playbook to automatically generate its supporting assets, including audiences, schemas, and journey templates.
t3: Publish the generated journey and audience assets to your sandbox to launch the loyalty re-engagement campaign.

title: Publish playbook assets to sandbox
t1: Create an instance of a playbook that generates schemas, datasets, and audiences for your use case.
t2: Review the playbook-generated assets and publish them to your development sandbox.
t3: Customize the published schemas and audiences in the development sandbox to fit your specific business needs.

title: Enable Playbooks catalog in new sandbox
t1: Create a new sandbox in Experience Platform to serve as the dedicated environment for Use Case Playbooks.
t2: Add the required user roles and permissions in the Admin Console to grant access to the Playbooks catalog in that sandbox.
t3: Open the Use Case Playbooks catalog in the configured sandbox to confirm the playbooks are visible and available.

title: Enrich profiles with partner propensity scores
t1: Match your first-party profiles with partner-provided propensity scores by ingesting partner attributes into Experience Platform.
t2: Enrich your customer profiles with those partner scores and build an audience segment based on the propensity thresholds.
t3: Activate the enriched audience to your advertising or marketing destinations for targeted campaign delivery.

title: Personalize landing page for unknown visitors
source: Partner Data / Personalize for unknown visitors
t1: Ingest partner-provided identity attributes for anonymous visitors to resolve who they are without requiring a login.
t2: Match those partner-resolved attributes to a real-time profile and qualify the anonymous visitor into a relevant audience segment.
t3: Serve a personalized landing page experience to the anonymous visitor based on their partner-resolved audience membership.

title: Partner data to DSP prospecting
t1: Ingest partner-provided prospect attributes and use them to build a lookalike audience of new potential customers in Real-Time CDP.
t2: Enrich the lookalike audience with partner data to validate quality and ensure the profiles meet your target customer criteria.
t3: Activate the partner-enriched lookalike audience to your DSP destination to run offsite prospecting campaigns.

title: Partner attributes for financial targeting
t1: Ingest partner-supplied income-band attributes into Experience Platform and map them to known customer profiles using shared identity keys.
t2: Enrich your real-time customer profiles by merging the partner income-band attributes with existing profile data via a merge policy.
t3: Build a financial product audience segmented by income band and activate it to your advertising or email destination for targeted offers.

title: Track profile completeness with dashboard
t1: Write a SQL query in Query Service to calculate the percentage of profiles that contain a valid email address.
t2: Save the query results as a dataset that can be used as a data source for a custom dashboard widget.
t3: Build a custom dashboard widget visualizing the profile email completeness percentage to monitor data quality over time.

title: Build destination health activation dashboard
t1: Create a custom dashboard and add widgets that query activation run data across your configured destinations.
t2: Configure each widget to display success and failure metrics broken down by channel, such as email, social, and display.
t3: Save and share the dashboard to monitor real-time activation success rates per channel for ongoing destination health visibility.

title: Monitor profile volume against entitlements
t1: Navigate to the License Usage dashboard to view your organization's current entitlement limits for profile volume and other metrics.
t2: Customize the dashboard by selecting the relevant metrics and time ranges to track profile count trends against your contracted limits.
t3: Review the visualized usage data regularly to identify when profile volume is approaching entitlement thresholds and take action accordingly.

title: Visualize propensity scores in dashboard
t1: Configure and run a Customer AI model to generate propensity scores for each customer profile.
t2: Create a custom Platform dashboard and add widgets that query the propensity score dataset.
t3: Visualize the propensity score distributions across your customer base directly in the custom dashboard.

title: Delete bad batch and re-ingest
t1: Identify the mis-mapped ingestion batch in the dataset activity view and submit a batch delete request to remove its records from the platform.
t2: Confirm the batch deletion has completed and verify that the incorrect records no longer appear in the dataset or unified profiles.
t3: Correct the source file mapping and re-ingest the updated file into the dataset to populate accurate records.

title: Schedule expiry for campaign event datasets
t1: Identify the time-boxed campaign event datasets that should be automatically removed after their retention period ends.
t2: Configure a dataset expiration schedule for each campaign dataset, specifying the exact expiry date in the Data Hygiene UI.
t3: Confirm the scheduled expirations so Platform automatically deletes each dataset when its expiry date is reached.

title: Audit and expire obsolete datasets
t1: Review dataset storage usage in Experience Platform to identify which datasets consume the most space.
t2: Flag large obsolete datasets that are no longer needed and mark them for expiration or deletion.
t3: Apply dataset expiration settings to remove the obsolete datasets and reclaim storage capacity.

title: Evaluate partner overlap before sharing
t1: Configure a Segment Match connection with a potential data partner to enable pre-share overlap estimation.
t2: Run overlap estimates to see how many profiles your audience shares with the partner's audience before committing to a share.
t3: Use the overlap results to decide whether the partner audience share is worth pursuing and proceed or decline accordingly.

title: Segment Match CPG brand partnership handshake
t1: Send a Segment Match connection request to the CPG brand partner using their IMS Organization ID.
t2: The CPG brand partner accepts the connection request, completing the mutual handshake in Segment Match.
t3: Share agreed-upon audience segments with the connected CPG partner for joint campaign targeting.

title: Review and accept partner audience share
t1: Open the incoming Segment Match feed and review the partner's data usage labels and governance terms attached to the shared audience.
t2: Verify that the partner's governance terms are compatible with your organization's data usage policies and confirm compliance.
t3: Accept the shared audience feed so the partner's audience becomes available for use in your sandbox.

title: Automate win-back journey by churn score
t1: Run Customer AI to generate churn propensity scores and create an audience of customers whose score exceeds the defined risk threshold.
t2: Configure a Journey Optimizer journey that triggers automatically when a customer enters that high-churn-score audience.
t3: Deliver a personalized win-back offer to each triggered customer across email and push channels within the journey.

title: Timed cart abandonment reminder journey
t1: Detect when a customer abandons their cart by capturing the real-time abandon event as a Journey Optimizer entry trigger.
t2: Build a journey that waits a set interval then sends a personalized cart reminder via email, followed by a push notification if unopened.
t3: Let the journey run and monitor open rates and conversions to optimize the timing and messaging of each reminder step.

title: Size and budget holiday campaign
source: Marketing Workflows / Plan and size campaign
t1: Use Segment Builder to define the holiday campaign audience and estimate its size across your customer base.
t2: Review the projected audience reach and confirm that the budget allocation aligns with the expected segment volume.
t3: Approve the finalized audience and budget plan, then launch the holiday campaign to the target audience.

title: Pull attribution metrics into PowerPoint
t1: Connect Adobe Marketing Agent to Customer Journey Analytics and pull attribution metrics for your campaign.
t2: Review the attribution data surfaced by the agent, confirming channel contributions and conversion insights.
t3: Export the attribution metrics from the agent directly into a PowerPoint deck for stakeholder reporting.

title: Onboard new loyalty programme members
t1: Configure a sign-up event trigger that fires when a customer enrolls in the loyalty programme.
t2: Build an onboarding journey in Journey Optimizer that starts when the sign-up event is received.
t3: Publish the journey so new members automatically receive a personalized welcome sequence across email and push channels.

title: AI scores drive homepage recommendations
t1: Configure and run a Customer AI model to generate propensity scores for each customer profile.
t2: Build an audience by segmenting profiles based on their Customer AI propensity score thresholds.
t3: Activate the audience to your homepage personalization destination to surface tailored product recommendations.

title: Score and activate travel upgrade audience
t1: Configure a Customer AI model with travel booking and loyalty data to score profiles for upgrade likelihood.
t2: Run the model to generate propensity scores and build an audience of the top-decile highest-scoring profiles.
t3: Activate the top-decile upgrade audience to your email or advertising destination for personalized offers.

title: Compare attribution models from AI outputs
t1: Configure and run an Attribution AI model instance to generate scores for your conversion events across touchpoints.
t2: Open the Attribution AI insights dashboard to review the data-driven attribution scores assigned to each marketing touchpoint.
t3: Compare those data-driven scores against the first-touch attribution view to identify which channels truly influence conversions.

title: Attribution insights drive budget reallocation
t1: Configure and run an Attribution AI model to score the contribution of each marketing touchpoint across your customer journeys.
t2: Analyze the Attribution AI insights dashboard to compare the actual revenue influence of display ads versus paid search channels.
t3: Use the channel performance evidence from Attribution AI to justify shifting budget away from display and into paid search.

title: Score profiles for subscription cancellation risk
t1: Configure a Customer AI instance by selecting subscription cancellation events as the prediction goal and defining the scoring population.
t2: Run the Customer AI model to generate churn propensity scores across all customer profiles.
t3: Use the generated scores to build audiences of at-risk customers for targeted retention campaigns.

title: Add user and assign platform role
t1: Add the business user to your Experience Platform product profile in the Adobe Admin Console.
t2: Once the user accepts the invitation and logs in, open the Permissions UI in Experience Platform.
t3: Assign the user to the appropriate role in Permissions to grant them the required access rights.

title: Grant marketer sandbox and audience access
t1: Add the marketer as a user in Adobe Admin Console and assign them to the Experience Platform product profile.
t2: In the Permissions UI, create or select a role that includes the target sandboxes and audience-builder feature permissions.
t3: Assign the marketer to that role so they can access the designated sandboxes and build audiences immediately.

title: Create role and provision analyst
t1: Create a new read-only reporting role in the Permissions UI and assign it view-only access to datasets, segments, and dashboards.
t2: Add the new data analyst as a user in the Admin Console so they have an Experience Platform account.
t3: Assign the read-only reporting role to that analyst in the Permissions UI so they can access reporting resources.

title: Provision Journey Optimizer journey authoring user
t1: Add the user to your organization in Adobe Admin Console so they have a valid account.
t2: Assign the user to the Journey Optimizer product profile that grants access to the application.
t3: In the Permissions UI, assign the journey-authoring role to grant the user the correct resource-level permissions.

title: Onboard developer with API credentials
t1: Add the developer to your organization in the Adobe Admin Console under the Experience Platform product profile.
t2: Create a new API credential project in Adobe Developer Console and link it to the Experience Platform product profile.
t3: Use the generated client ID, client secret, and private key to authenticate and call Experience Platform APIs.

title: Grant developer API access via role
t1: Add the developer to your organization in the Admin Console and generate their API credentials.
t2: Assign the developer's API credentials to the appropriate role in the Permissions UI.
t3: The role grants the developer access to the designated sandboxes and sources through their API credentials.

title: Grant engineer API access to platform
t1: Add the data engineer as a developer to the AEP product profile in Adobe Admin Console.
t2: Assign the engineer a role with Sources and Destinations API permissions in the Experience Platform Permissions UI.
t3: The engineer generates API credentials from the Developer Console to authenticate calls to the Sources and Destinations APIs.

title: Promote user to platform admin
t1: Locate the experienced platform user in the Adobe Admin Console under the Experience Platform product.
t2: Add the user to the product administrator role for Experience Platform in the Admin Console.
t3: Confirm the user now has admin access by verifying their elevated permissions in the Experience Platform Permissions UI.

title: Delegate admin rights to team lead
t1: In the Adobe Admin Console, add the platform team lead as a product administrator for Adobe Experience Platform.
t2: Log in to the Experience Platform Permissions UI and confirm the team lead account appears with administrative access.
t3: Assign the team lead to the appropriate roles so they can manage permissions for their team members.

title: Restrict PHI fields from agency users
t1: Apply data usage labels to sensitive protected health information fields in the schema to mark them as restricted.
t2: Create a role for external agency users that explicitly excludes permissions to view or access those labeled PHI fields.
t3: Assign the external agency users to that role, preventing them from accessing the protected health information fields.

title: Label PHI fields and restrict access
t1: Apply PHI data usage labels to sensitive health-related fields in your schema to mark them as restricted.
t2: Create an attribute-based access control policy that blocks access to any fields carrying those PHI labels.
t3: Assign roles to users who should not see health data, ensuring the policy prevents them from viewing those labeled fields.

title: Restrict access to financial PII fields
t1: Apply data usage labels to regulated financial PII schema fields to mark them as sensitive and restricted.
t2: Create an access control policy that blocks roles without explicit permission from viewing those labeled fields.
t3: Assign only authorized roles to the policy so permitted users can access the fields while all others are denied.

title: Label consent field and enforce access
t1: Apply a GDPR-restricted data usage label to the consent schema field to mark it as sensitive.
t2: Create an access control policy that denies access to any fields carrying that label.
t3: Assign the policy to a role so users in that role are blocked from viewing or activating the restricted consent field.

title: Develop and promote sandbox configurations
t1: Create a new development sandbox to safely build and test your configurations without affecting production.
t2: Package the tested configurations into a sandbox package and publish it for export.
t3: Import the published package into the production sandbox to promote the validated configurations.

title: Test schema and pipeline in sandbox
t1: Create a non-production sandbox to isolate testing from your live production environment.
t2: Build and deploy a new schema and ingestion pipeline inside that sandbox to validate data flows safely.
t3: Promote the validated schema and pipeline configuration to the production environment once testing is complete.

title: Sandbox setup for regional business unit
t1: Create a new sandbox in the Admin Console and assign it a name that identifies the regional business unit.
t2: Grant the regional team's user group access to the sandbox by assigning the appropriate roles and permissions.
t3: Configure the sandbox with the schemas, datasets, and destinations required by the regional business unit.

title: Set Up Playbooks Inspiration Sandbox
t1: Create a new sandbox in the Admin console and designate it as an inspiration sandbox for Use Case Playbooks exploration.
t2: Navigate to the Use Case Playbooks gallery within the inspiration sandbox and browse available playbooks.
t3: Create a playbook instance and publish its generated assets into the inspiration sandbox for review.

title: Reset sandbox between project phases
t1: Navigate to the Sandboxes section in the Admin UI and select the development sandbox you want to reset.
t2: Trigger the sandbox reset to delete all assets, schemas, datasets, and profiles within that sandbox.
t3: Confirm the reset is complete and begin rebuilding the sandbox configuration for the new project phase.

title: Promote campaign config to production
t1: Package the tested campaign configuration artifacts in the development sandbox into a sandbox tooling package.
t2: Publish the package and import it into the production sandbox using the sandbox tooling copy workflow.
t3: Verify the campaign configuration is intact in production and activate it for live use.

title: Replicate journey assets across sandboxes
t1: Package a journey along with its dependent audiences and schemas into a sandbox tooling export in the source sandbox.
t2: Publish the package to make it available for import into another sandbox.
t3: Import the published package into the target sandbox to recreate the journey and all its dependencies without manual recreation.

title: Migrate schemas and datasets across sandboxes
t1: In the staging sandbox, create a package containing the validated schemas and datasets you want to migrate.
t2: Publish the package to make it available for import into another sandbox.
t3: Import the published package into the production sandbox to replicate the schemas and datasets.

title: Deploy audience activation flow to production
t1: Package the complete audience activation flow, including schemas, datasets, segments, and destinations, into a sandbox package in the development sandbox.
t2: Publish the sandbox package and export it so it is ready for import into another sandbox environment.
t3: Import the published package into the production sandbox to deploy the full audience activation flow.

title: Copy governance schema to regional sandbox
t1: Package the governance-approved data schema in the source sandbox using the Sandbox Tooling export feature.
t2: Publish the package to make it available for import into another sandbox.
t3: Import the published package into the target regional sandbox to replicate the approved schema.

title: Share journey config with partner org
source: Sandbox Tooling / Share packages across orgs
t1: Package the customer success journey configuration, including schemas, datasets, and journey assets, into a sandbox package.
t2: Publish the package and share it with the partner Adobe org using cross-org package sharing.
t3: The partner org imports the package into their sandbox to deploy the customer success journey configuration.

title: Share compliance audience model across orgs
source: Sandbox Tooling / Share packages across orgs
t1: Package the compliance-approved audience model and its dependent assets into a sandbox tooling package.
t2: Publish the package and share it with the target IMS organizations via the cross-org sharing feature.
t3: Each recipient org imports the package into their sandbox, making the audience model available for activation.

title: Share campaign config across orgs
source: Sandbox Tooling / Share packages across orgs
t1: Package the co-branded campaign configuration, including schemas and audiences, into a sandbox package.
t2: Publish the package and generate a shareable link to distribute it to the partner organization.
t3: Import the shared package into the partner org's sandbox to replicate the campaign configuration.

title: Model loyalty data with XDM profile
t1: Create an XDM Individual Profile schema in the Schema Editor to represent your customer loyalty data structure.
t2: Add identity fields such as email or loyalty ID to the schema and mark them as primary and secondary identities.
t3: Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so loyalty data can be merged into unified customer profiles.

title: XDM schema for web clickstream
t1: Create a new XDM Experience Event schema in the Schema Editor to capture web clickstream behavior.
t2: Add the required field groups, such as Web Details and Environment Details, to include clickstream-specific fields.
t3: Save and enable the schema so datasets can be created from it to ingest web interaction data.

title: Mobile app event schema with identity
t1: Create an XDM Experience Event schema and add the Mobile App Details and Environment field groups to capture mobile app interaction events.
t2: Add the Identity Map field group to the schema to store device identifiers such as IDFA and GAID for identity resolution.
t3: Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so mobile app events are stitched into unified profiles using those device identities.

title: Build B2C profile schema with identities
t1: Create an XDM Individual Profile schema for your B2C brand and add the required field groups for personal details and CRM attributes.
t2: Define email address and CRM ID fields as identity descriptors, setting one as the primary identity for profile stitching.
t3: Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so ingested records merge into unified customer profiles.

title: In-store purchase event schema setup
t1: Create an XDM ExperienceEvent schema and add the Commerce Details field group to capture transaction data like purchase amount and items.
t2: Add the IdentityMap field group and define loyalty card ID and email as identity fields to link the event to a customer profile.
t3: Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so ingested in-store purchase events contribute to unified customer profiles.

title: Add subscription status field group
t1: Create a custom field group defining subscription status fields such as plan type, renewal date, and opt-in flag.
t2: Add the new custom field group to your existing profile schema in the Schema Editor.
t3: Save the updated schema so subscription status fields are available for data ingestion and profile attributes.

title: Extend schema with loyalty tier fields
t1: Create a custom field group defining company-specific loyalty tier attributes such as tier name, points balance, and enrollment date.
t2: Add the custom field group to your standard Individual Profile schema to extend it with those loyalty tier fields.
t3: Save the updated schema so that datasets and profiles can capture and store loyalty tier data for your customers.

title: Custom consent field group for GDPR
t1: Create a custom field group in the Schema Editor and add consent and preference fields required for GDPR compliance.
t2: Add the custom consent field group to your XDM Individual Profile schema and save the schema.
t3: Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so that consent preferences are captured and enforced on every unified customer profile.

title: Add propensity score field group to schema
t1: Create a custom field group containing AI propensity score attributes such as churn likelihood and purchase probability.
t2: Add the custom field group to an existing XDM Individual Profile schema in the Schema Editor.
t3: Save the updated schema so propensity score attributes are available for ingestion and segmentation in Real-Time Customer Profile.

title: Custom class for product catalog
t1: Create a custom XDM class to represent the new product entity type, defining its core identity and behavior.
t2: Create a schema that uses the new custom class as its base structure for the product catalog.
t3: Add field groups to the schema to capture all required product attributes and relationships.

title: Reusable address type across schemas
t1: Create a reusable structured address data type with fields like street, city, state, and postal code.
t2: Add the address data type to a customer profile schema to capture residential address information.
t3: Add the same address data type to an order schema to capture shipping and billing addresses.

title: Link product catalog to profile schema
t1: Define a reference field on the product catalog schema that will serve as the join key to the customer profile schema.
t2: Open the relationship editor and configure the reference field to point to the primary identity of the customer profile schema.
t3: Save the relationship so the product catalog schema is linked and can be used in segmentation and queries alongside customer profiles.

title: Join order events to profile schema
t1: Define a source schema for order events and a destination schema for profiles, ensuring both have a primary identity field configured.
t2: In the source order event schema, add a relationship descriptor that references the primary identity field of the destination profile schema.
t3: Save the relationship so that Query Service and Customer Journey Analytics can join order event records to their corresponding profile records.

title: Model B2B account opportunity data
t1: Create a B2B Account schema using the XDM Business Account class to capture company-level attributes for ABM targeting.
t2: Create a B2B Opportunity schema using the XDM Business Opportunity class and link it to the Account schema via a relationship field.
t3: Enable both schemas for Real-Time Customer Profile so account and opportunity data can be unified and used in ABM campaigns.

title: Link Account and Contact B2B schemas
t1: Create an Account schema using the XDM Business Account class to represent your B2B account records.
t2: Create a Contact schema using the XDM Business Contact class to represent individuals associated with accounts.
t3: Define a relationship field on the Contact schema that references the Account schema to link contacts to their accounts.

title: Copy production schema to regional sandbox
t1: Finalize the production schema by ensuring all required field groups are added and the schema is fully configured.
t2: Package the schema using the sandbox tooling, bundling all associated field groups into an exportable package.
t3: Import the package into the target regional sandbox to recreate the schema with all its field groups intact.

title: Add consent field to profile schema
t1: Open the existing customer profile schema in the Schema Editor and add a new field for opt-in consent using the appropriate data type.
t2: Assign the new consent field to the correct field group and save the updated schema definition.
t3: Verify the updated schema is reflected in the associated dataset so incoming consent data maps to the new field correctly.

title: Extend schema with custom field group
t1: Create a custom field group containing purchase preference attributes such as preferred category, price range, and brand affinity.
t2: Add the custom field group to the existing schema by editing the schema in the Schema Editor.
t3: Save the updated schema so downstream datasets and profiles can capture the new purchase preference attributes.

title: CSV records to unified profiles
t1: Upload a CSV file of customer records to Experience Platform using the batch ingestion workflow.
t2: Map the CSV fields to an XDM schema and complete the batch ingestion job to create a dataset.
t3: Enable the dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile so ingested records merge into unified profiles.

title: Daily CRM export to profile dataset
t1: Upload the daily CRM export file to a Platform dataset by creating a batch and posting the file via the batch ingestion API.
t2: Close and finalize the batch so Platform validates and ingests the records into the dataset.
t3: Confirm the ingested records are merged into Real-Time Customer Profile by verifying profile counts in the monitoring dashboard.

title: FTP loyalty data to Platform
t1: Connect the FTP landing zone as a source connector in Experience Platform to access the weekly loyalty tier update files.
t2: Map the FTP file fields to your loyalty schema and ingest the batch data into the corresponding Platform dataset.
t3: Verify the batch ingestion run succeeded and confirm updated loyalty tier records appear in customer profiles.

title: Parquet file to customer dataset
t1: Upload a Parquet file containing customer attribute updates to Experience Platform using the batch ingestion API.
t2: Monitor the batch ingestion job to confirm the file is successfully processed and validated.
t3: Verify the ingested records appear in the target Platform dataset with updated customer attributes.

title: Stream checkout events into Platform
t1: Register a streaming inlet using the HTTP API Source to create an authenticated endpoint for your mobile app.
t2: Send real-time checkout event payloads from the mobile app to that streaming endpoint using HTTP POST requests.
t3: Verify the streamed events land in the Platform dataset and are merged into real-time customer profiles.

title: Stream POS events into Platform
t1: Connect your retail point-of-sale systems to Platform using the Streaming Ingestion API or an HTTP Source connector.
t2: Stream transaction events in real time so Platform ingests each sale as it occurs at the register.
t3: Verify the incoming data in the dataset activity view to confirm records are landing correctly in Platform.

title: Stream search events to Platform
t1: Instrument your website with the Web SDK to capture real-time search behavior events as they occur.
t2: The Web SDK sends those events to the Edge Network, which forwards them to Experience Platform as a streaming data flow.
t3: The streamed events land in a dataset and update Real-Time Customer Profiles with the latest search behavior.

title: Collect web events via Edge Network
t1: Install and configure the AEP Web SDK on your website to capture page view and cart events from visitors.
t2: The Web SDK sends those events in real time through the Edge Network, which validates and routes the data to Experience Platform.
t3: The ingested events land in your configured dataset and are merged into real-time customer profiles for immediate use.

title: Analytics report suite to XDM
t1: Connect an Adobe Analytics report suite to Experience Platform using the Analytics source connector.
t2: Map the Analytics dimensions and metrics to their corresponding XDM fields in the data mapping step.
t3: Activate the dataflow so that report suite data streams into a dataset as XDM-formatted records.

title: Audience Manager segments into Platform datasets
source: Data Ingestion / Ingest from Audience Manager
t1: Connect Adobe Audience Manager as a source to begin streaming segments and traits into Experience Platform.
t2: Map the incoming Audience Manager traits and segments to an XDM schema for standardized data representation.
t3: Verify the mapped data lands in an Experience Platform dataset ready for profile and segmentation use.

title: Sync Marketo leads into Platform
t1: Configure the Marketo source connector by authenticating with your Munchkin ID and mapping lead and activity objects to XDM schemas.
t2: Run the dataflow to ingest Marketo lead and activity records into Platform datasets in batch or streaming mode.
t3: Verify that the ingested records are merged into unified Real-Time Customer Profiles via the identity graph.

title: Schedule S3 transaction files to dataset
source: Data Ingestion / Ingest from cloud storage
t1: Connect your Amazon S3 bucket as a source in Experience Platform and select the daily transaction files to ingest.
t2: Map the source file fields to your target XDM schema and configure a recurring daily dataflow schedule.
t3: Run the scheduled dataflow to load each day's transaction files into the target Platform dataset automatically.

title: Connect Salesforce CRM to Platform
t1: Configure a Salesforce CRM source connector by authenticating with your Salesforce credentials and selecting the contact object to ingest.
t2: Map the Salesforce contact fields to their corresponding XDM schema fields using the field mapping interface.
t3: Run the dataflow to ingest the mapped Salesforce contact records into your Platform dataset.

title: PostgreSQL database to Platform nightly
t1: Connect your PostgreSQL database to Experience Platform by configuring a source connector with your credentials.
t2: Map the database table fields to your target XDM schema to define how the data will land in Platform.
t3: Schedule a nightly incremental dataflow so only new or updated records are ingested into Platform automatically.

title: Stream events via HTTP API inlet
source: Data Ingestion / Stream via HTTP API
t1: Create a streaming HTTP API inlet in Experience Platform to generate a unique endpoint URL for receiving data.
t2: POST JSON event payloads to that endpoint URL from your application or server in real time.
t3: Experience Platform processes the incoming events and immediately updates the matching real-time customer profiles.

title: Stream third-party events into Platform
t1: Configure a third-party streaming source connector by providing authentication credentials and selecting the target dataflow.
t2: Map the incoming event fields from the source schema to your Platform XDM schema so data lands correctly.
t3: Activate the dataflow to begin streaming real-time events into your Platform datasets for immediate profile updates.

title: Monitor and resolve failed batch ingestion
t1: Ingest a batch of customer data into Experience Platform and open the monitoring dashboard to track its progress.
t2: Identify the failed batch job in the dashboard by reviewing the error details and failure reason provided.
t3: Correct the data issues in the source file and re-ingest the batch to complete successful ingestion.

title: Label identity fields in profile schema
t1: Open your profile schema in the Schema Editor and select the email, phone, and CRM ID fields you want to designate as identities.
t2: Mark each selected field as an identity field and assign the appropriate identity namespace, such as Email, Phone, or a custom CRM ID namespace.
t3: Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so the labeled identity fields are used to stitch records into unified profiles via the identity graph.

title: Set loyalty ID as primary identity
t1: Open your loyalty schema in the Schema Editor and mark the loyalty program ID field as the primary identity namespace.
t2: Locate the email field in the same schema and label it as a secondary identity namespace.
t3: Save the schema so Experience Platform uses the loyalty ID to anchor unified profiles and email as a supporting identity link.

title: Set ECID as primary identity
t1: Create an Experience Event schema in the Schema Editor and add the ECID field from the Experience Cloud ID namespace.
t2: Mark the ECID field as the primary identity on the schema to designate it as the main identifier for events.
t3: Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so incoming events are stitched into unified profiles using the ECID.

title: Ingest data to build identity graph
t1: Ingest customer records containing multiple identity fields such as email, phone, and CRM ID into Experience Platform.
t2: Identity Service processes the ingested data and links the identity fields into a unified identity graph for each customer.
t3: Use the identity graph to merge profile fragments into a single real-time customer profile across all touchpoints.

title: Stitch web, mobile, CRM identities
t1: Ingest customer data from your website, mobile app, and CRM, each carrying their own identifiers such as cookies, device IDs, and email addresses.
t2: Identity Service links those identifiers across sources into a single identity graph, resolving all fragments to one unified customer profile.
t3: Query the identity graph to trace a customer's full cross-channel journey using any known identifier as the starting point.

title: Link anonymous visitor to known profile
t1: Capture an anonymous visitor's web interactions using the Web SDK, assigning them a temporary ECID.
t2: When the visitor logs in, send their authenticated identity so the identity graph links the ECID to their known Customer ID.
t3: Experience Platform merges the anonymous and authenticated profiles into a single unified real-time customer profile.

title: Merge device ID at app login
t1: Capture the anonymous mobile device ID collected during pre-login app browsing as an identity in the identity graph.
t2: When the customer logs into the app, link the mobile device ID to their authenticated customer ID via Identity Service.
t3: Identity Service merges the anonymous device activity into the existing customer profile, creating a complete unified view.

title: Resolve guest checkout to known profile
t1: Capture the anonymous visitor's browsing session under a temporary ECID during guest checkout.
t2: At order confirmation, collect the customer's email address and send it to Identity Service alongside the ECID.
t3: Identity Service stitches the email to the existing ECID, merging the anonymous session into the known customer profile.

title: Verify VIP customer cross-channel identities
t1: Search for the VIP customer in Identity Service by entering one of their known identifiers, such as email or CRM ID.
t2: Open the identity graph viewer to see all identities linked to that customer across channels and devices.
t3: Confirm that all expected cross-channel identifiers, such as mobile ID, web cookie, and loyalty ID, are correctly stitched together in the graph.

title: Enable CRM Dataset for Unified Profiles
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Bring data into profile
t1: Ingest your CRM records into a dataset built on a schema with the correct identity fields defined.
t2: Enable the dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile so ingested records are merged into unified profiles.
t3: Verify that the CRM records appear as unified customer profiles in the Profile viewer.

title: Enable loyalty dataset for profile
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Bring data into profile
t1: Create a schema for loyalty transaction data and enable it for Real-Time Customer Profile.
t2: Create a dataset using that schema and ingest loyalty transaction records into it.
t3: Enable the dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile so loyalty data enriches unified customer profiles.

title: Mobile events to unified profile
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Bring data into profile
t1: Instrument your mobile app with the Mobile SDK to stream real-time event data into Experience Platform.
t2: Map the incoming event data to an XDM schema and ingest it into a Profile-enabled dataset.
t3: Experience Platform stitches the mobile events into unified real-time customer profiles ready for personalization.

title: Merge policy prioritizing CRM data
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Create merge policies
t1: Navigate to the Merge Policies section in the Real-Time Customer Profile settings and create a new merge policy.
t2: Configure the merge policy to use a custom dataset precedence order, placing your CRM dataset above any third-party data datasets.
t3: Save and set the merge policy as active so unified profiles are built using CRM data as the authoritative source.

title: Merge policy for B2B account profiles
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Create merge policies
t1: Enable your B2B account datasets for Real-Time Customer Profile so their data is available for merging.
t2: Create a new merge policy and set the merge method to dataset precedence, ordering your B2B account datasets by priority.
t3: Apply the merge policy to your account profile view so that profile lookups reflect the correct dataset precedence.

title: Last-write-wins merge policy setup
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Create merge policies
t1: Create a merge policy in the Profile settings and select timestamp-ordered last-write-wins as the attribute merge method.
t2: Assign the relevant union schema and enable the merge policy as the default for your streaming ingestion datasets.
t3: Verify that incoming streaming records update unified profiles correctly by checking that the most recent attribute values always take precedence.

title: Sum purchases with computed attribute
t1: Define a computed attribute in the Profile UI that sums the total purchase amount from experience events in the last 30 days.
t2: Enable and publish the computed attribute so Platform continuously calculates and updates the value on each customer profile.
t3: Use the computed attribute as a condition in Segment Builder to build audiences based on each customer's rolling 30-day spend.

title: Track app sessions with computed attribute
t1: Define a computed attribute that counts the number of app session events occurring in the past 7 days.
t2: Publish the computed attribute so it continuously updates on each customer's real-time profile.
t3: Use the computed attribute in Segment Builder to create audiences based on recent app session activity.

title: Compute recency score from purchase events
t1: Define a computed attribute rule that calculates a recency score based on the customer's last purchase event date.
t2: Enable and publish the computed attribute so it is continuously evaluated and appended to each customer's real-time profile.
t3: Use the recency score attribute in Segment Builder to create audiences targeting customers by how recently they purchased.

title: Delete former customer profile data
t1: Identify the former customer's identity namespace and identity value to target their profile for deletion.
t2: Submit a profile delete job via the Profile System Jobs API using the customer's identity details.
t3: Monitor the delete job status until it completes, confirming the customer's data is removed from the profile store.

title: Upsert email opt-out preference field
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Update profile attributes
t1: Identify the customer's profile by their identity namespace and ID to target the correct record.
t2: Send a Profile Upsert API request with the updated email opt-out preference field value for that customer.
t3: Verify the unified profile now reflects the new opt-out preference in Real-Time Customer Profile.

title: Revoke consent via profile upsert
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Update profile attributes
t1: Receive a customer's consent revocation event and prepare the updated consent attributes for ingestion.
t2: Send an API upsert call to the Real-Time Customer Profile endpoint to immediately overwrite the stored consent fields.
t3: Verify the profile reflects the revoked consent so downstream journeys and activations respect the updated preference.

title: Explore union schema for segmentation
t1: Enable your XDM schemas for Real-Time Customer Profile so their fields contribute to the union schema.
t2: Navigate to the Union Schema view in the platform to see all merged attributes across every enabled schema for a given class.
t3: Use those discovered attributes to define precise segment conditions in the Segment Builder.

title: Target viewers who skipped purchase
t1: Define a segment rule that includes customers who viewed a product page within a recent time window.
t2: Add an exclusion rule to filter out any customers who completed a purchase for that product.
t3: Save and activate the resulting audience to re-engage those browsing customers across your channels.

title: Segment high-value customers by spend
t1: Open Segment Builder and add the lifetime spend attribute with a threshold rule to filter high-value customers.
t2: Preview the estimated audience size to confirm the threshold captures the right customer segment.
t3: Save and publish the audience so it is available for activation to downstream destinations.

title: Segment email openers last week
t1: Open Segment Builder and add an event rule filtering for email open events within the last 7 days.
t2: Review the estimated audience size to confirm the rule captures the right customers.
t3: Save and publish the audience for use in campaigns or journeys.

title: Churn-risk audience from purchase recency
t1: Open Segment Builder and add a days-since-last-purchase attribute rule, setting a threshold that identifies customers who have not purchased recently.
t2: Review the estimated audience size to confirm the rule captures the intended churn-risk population, then save the segment definition.
t3: Publish the churn-risk audience so it is available for activation in re-engagement journeys and campaigns.

title: Re-engage inactive loyalty members
t1: Define a segment rule that filters for loyalty program members using their profile attributes.
t2: Add a behavioral condition to exclude any member who has visited the site in the last 60 days.
t3: Save the audience and activate it to a re-engagement channel to bring inactive members back.

title: Propensity score to targeted audience
t1: Configure and run a Customer AI model to generate propensity scores for each customer profile.
t2: Open Segment Builder and add a propensity score condition with a threshold above your defined value.
t3: Save the segment to create an audience of high-propensity customers ready for activation.

title: Holiday campaign audience from purchase history
t1: Ingest both in-store and online purchase history data into Experience Platform and merge them into unified real-time customer profiles.
t2: Open Segment Builder and define rules that combine in-store purchase attributes with online purchase events to identify holiday shoppers.
t3: Save and publish the audience for activation in your holiday campaign channels.

title: B2B accounts with large open opportunities
t1: Connect your CRM and ingest account and opportunity data into Experience Platform using a B2B source connector.
t2: In Segment Builder, filter accounts linked to open opportunities where the deal size exceeds your defined revenue threshold.
t3: Save and activate the B2B account audience to your sales engagement or advertising destination.

title: Real-time browsing to product segment
t1: Stream page-view events from the website into Experience Platform using the Web SDK as customers browse.
t2: Evaluate incoming events against a product-interest segment rule in real time using streaming segmentation.
t3: Qualify customers into the segment instantly and activate the updated audience to a personalization destination.

title: Add to cart triggers push notification
t1: Define a streaming segment that qualifies customers the moment they add an item to their cart.
t2: The customer adds an item to their cart, triggering instant audience qualification in real time.
t3: Fire a push notification to the qualified customer immediately, driving them back to complete their purchase.

title: Stream session end into re-engagement
t1: Capture a real-time session-end event with no purchase via the Web SDK as a streaming event into Experience Platform.
t2: A streaming segment rule evaluates the event instantly and qualifies the customer for the re-engagement audience in real time.
t3: Trigger a re-engagement journey that delivers a personalized message to the customer immediately after their session ends.

title: Real-time VIP segment on spend
t1: Define a streaming segment rule that qualifies customers whose cumulative spend crosses your VIP threshold in real time.
t2: As a customer's next purchase pushes their total spend over the threshold, the streaming engine instantly adds them to the VIP segment.
t3: Activate the VIP audience to your personalization and loyalty destinations to immediately deliver VIP-tier experiences.

title: On-demand batch audience for weather campaign
t1: Create a new audience segment targeting customers likely to respond to a weather-related product promotion.
t2: Trigger an on-demand batch segmentation job to immediately evaluate and populate the audience without waiting for the scheduled run.
t3: Activate the freshly evaluated audience to your campaign destination to launch the urgent weather-related promotion.

title: On-demand batch evaluation for flash sale
t1: Open the audience in Segment Builder and trigger a manual on-demand batch evaluation job to refresh membership ahead of schedule.
t2: Wait for the evaluation job to complete and verify the updated audience membership counts reflect current customer data.
t3: Activate the freshly evaluated audience to your destination to power the unexpected flash-sale campaign immediately.

title: Share audiences with retail partner
t1: Configure a Segment Match connection by sending a connection request to your retail partner using their IMS org ID.
t2: Once the partner accepts the connection, select the audience segments you want to share and define the match keys for identity overlap.
t3: Publish the Segment Match feed so your retail partner can receive and activate the shared audience in their sandbox.

title: Share buyer audience via Segment Match
t1: Create a high-intent buyer audience in Segment Builder using behavioral and purchase signals.
t2: Set up a Segment Match connection by sending a feed invitation to your media partner organization.
t3: Share the high-intent buyer audience through the accepted Segment Match feed for the partner to activate.

title: Partner segment to prospecting campaign
t1: Accept an incoming Segment Match share from a CPG partner to receive their audience data into your sandbox.
t2: Combine the received partner segment with your own profile data to build a refined prospecting audience.
t3: Activate the prospecting audience to your advertising destination to launch a targeted prospecting campaign.

title: Set Up Facebook Custom Audiences Destination
t1: Navigate to the Destinations catalog and select Facebook Custom Audiences, then authenticate by connecting your Facebook ad account.
t2: Configure the destination by specifying the account ID, data mapping, and identity fields to match Platform profiles to Facebook users.
t3: Save the configured destination so it is available to receive and activate audiences from Platform.

title: Connect Platform to Google Ads
t1: Navigate to the Destinations catalog and select Google Ads to begin configuring the connection with your account credentials.
t2: Authenticate and configure the destination by mapping your first-party identity fields to the Google Ads customer match parameters.
t3: Activate your first-party audience to the connected Google Ads destination to enable targeted ad delivery.

title: LinkedIn destination for B2B targeting
t1: Authenticate and configure a LinkedIn Matched Audiences destination connection in the Destinations catalog.
t2: Map your account-based audience segments to the LinkedIn destination, matching profile attributes to LinkedIn's required identity fields.
t3: Activate the mapped B2B audiences to LinkedIn so matched accounts receive targeted advertising campaigns.

title: Activate high-value audience to email
t1: Build a high-value customer audience using profile attributes and purchase behavior in Segment Builder.
t2: Connect your email service provider as a destination in Experience Platform.
t3: Activate the high-value audience to that email destination to launch your campaign.

title: Activate churn-risk audience to CRM
t1: Build a churn-risk audience by segmenting profiles that show high likelihood of churning based on behavioral signals.
t2: Connect your CRM platform as a destination in Experience Platform and configure the field mappings.
t3: Activate the churn-risk audience to the CRM destination so your retention team can launch targeted outreach campaigns.

title: Cart abandoners to display ads
t1: Build a cart abandonment audience by segmenting profiles of customers who added items but did not complete checkout.
t2: Connect a programmatic display advertising destination and configure the mapping and activation settings.
t3: Activate the cart abandonment audience to that destination to serve targeted display ads to those shoppers.

title: Export raw events to Azure Data Lake
t1: Connect an Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 destination in Experience Platform using your account credentials.
t2: Select the raw events dataset you want to export and map it to the connected Azure Data Lake destination.
t3: Schedule and run the dataset export so the raw events land in Azure Data Lake for downstream analysis.

title: Nightly profile data to cloud storage
t1: Connect a cloud storage destination by providing your bucket credentials and authentication details in the Destinations catalog.
t2: Select the profile attribute dataset you want to export and map the relevant fields to the destination schema.
t3: Configure a nightly export schedule so Platform automatically delivers the profile attribute data to your cloud storage bucket each night.

title: Export audiences to Azure Blob
t1: Connect to the Azure Blob destination by providing your storage account credentials and container details.
t2: Configure a scheduled export by setting the file format, export frequency, and file naming conventions for the audience data.
t3: Activate your target audience to the Azure Blob destination so membership exports are delivered to your container on schedule.

title: Sync B2B audience to Marketo
t1: Build a high-intent B2B audience in Real-Time CDP by segmenting profiles based on product engagement and firmographic attributes.
t2: Connect Marketo Engage as a destination and map the audience fields to the corresponding Marketo lead attributes.
t3: Activate the audience to Marketo Engage so matched leads automatically enroll in the appropriate nurturing sequences.

title: First-party email audience to Google
t1: Build an audience of known customers using their hashed email addresses in Real-Time CDP.
t2: Connect to the Google Customer Match destination and map the hashed email identity field.
t3: Activate the audience to Google Customer Match to enable search retargeting for those customers.

title: Seed audience to Facebook prospecting
t1: Build a seed audience of your highest-value existing customers using profile attributes and behaviors in Segment Builder.
t2: Connect your Facebook Ads account as a destination and activate the seed audience to Facebook Custom Audiences.
t3: Facebook uses the seed audience to generate a lookalike audience, expanding your reach to new prospective customers.

title: Activate audience via LiveRamp CTV
t1: Connect the LiveRamp destination in Experience Platform and authenticate with your LiveRamp account credentials.
t2: Select your first-party audience and activate it to the LiveRamp destination for identity resolution and distribution.
t3: LiveRamp distributes the resolved audience to connected TV and addressable media partners for targeted campaign delivery.

title: Share audience to Snowflake data science
t1: Build and save a Platform audience of the customers you want to share with the data science team.
t2: Configure a Snowflake batch data share destination and connect it to your Platform instance.
t3: Activate the audience to the Snowflake destination so the data science team can query it directly.

title: Personalize homepage for high-value segment
t1: Build a high-value customer audience in Real-Time CDP using profile attributes and behavioral data.
t2: Connect Adobe Target as a destination and activate the high-value audience to it.
t3: Configure a Target activity to deliver personalized homepage content to visitors who match that audience.

title: Profile attributes to Target recommendations
t1: Connect Adobe Target as a destination in Real-Time CDP and enable profile attribute sharing.
t2: Build an audience in Real-Time CDP that includes the product affinity and behavioral attributes you want to use.
t3: Activate the audience to Adobe Target so those profile attributes power personalized product recommendations on your site.

title: Customer AI churn model to audience
t1: Configure and train a Customer AI model to predict churn propensity scores for each customer profile.
t2: Once scoring is complete, build a segment targeting customers with high churn propensity scores.
t3: Activate the high-risk audience to your preferred channel to deliver a personalized win-back offer.

title: Customer AI purchase propensity to activation
t1: Configure a Customer AI model by selecting the purchase outcome, input datasets, and scoring schedule, then run the model to generate propensity scores.
t2: Build an audience in Segment Builder by filtering profiles with a high purchase propensity score above your chosen threshold.
t3: Activate the high-intent audience to your advertising or email destination to deliver personalized campaigns.

title: Score profiles and target upsell
t1: Configure a Customer AI model to predict upsell likelihood and run it against your ingested customer profiles.
t2: Build an audience in Segment Builder using the propensity scores generated by Customer AI to target high-likelihood upsell candidates.
t3: Activate that audience to your email or advertising destination to deliver a personalized upsell campaign.

title: Churn prediction to retention journey
t1: Configure and run a Customer AI model to generate churn propensity scores for each customer profile.
t2: Build an audience of high-churn-risk customers by filtering profiles where the propensity score exceeds your defined threshold.
t3: Activate that audience in a Journey Optimizer campaign to deliver personalized retention offers before those customers churn.

title: Score and retarget app-uninstall risk users
t1: Configure a Customer AI model with app engagement data, setting app uninstall as the prediction outcome.
t2: Run the Customer AI model to generate propensity scores indicating each user's uninstall risk.
t3: Build an audience in Segment Builder by filtering profiles with high uninstall-risk propensity scores.
t4: Activate the at-risk audience to advertising and push notification destinations to retarget those users.

title: Measure Channel ROI with Attribution AI
t1: Define conversion events in Attribution AI by specifying the goal actions such as purchases or sign-ups you want to measure.
t2: Map your marketing touchpoints to the conversion events to identify which channels influenced each conversion.
t3: Configure and run the Attribution AI model to generate attribution scores across all mapped touchpoints and channels.
t4: Analyze the attribution scores and channel ROI insights in the dashboard to optimize your marketing spend allocation.

title: Attribution AI to budget reallocation
t1: Configure an Attribution AI model instance by selecting your conversion events and mapping your marketing touchpoint datasets.
t2: Run the Attribution AI model to generate algorithmic credit scores across all marketing channels and touchpoints.
t3: Analyze the channel performance insights dashboard to identify which channels drive the most conversion credit.
t4: Reallocate your marketing budget toward the highest-performing channels based on the Attribution AI scores.

title: Attribution AI scores to executive dashboard
t1: Configure an Attribution AI model instance by selecting your conversion events and specifying the lookback window and attribution model type.
t2: Run the Attribution AI model to generate channel and touchpoint influence scores across your customer journeys.
t3: Export the Attribution AI scores dataset to Customer Journey Analytics by connecting it as a CJA data source.
t4: Build an executive dashboard in CJA using the attribution scores to visualize channel performance and marketing ROI.

title: Query datasets for channel visitor counts
t1: Navigate to Query Service in Experience Platform and open the Query Editor to begin writing SQL.
t2: Write a SQL query that selects the marketing channel field and counts distinct visitor IDs from your experience event dataset.
t3: Run the query to execute it against the Platform dataset and retrieve the unique visitor counts grouped by marketing channel.
t4: Review the results table in the Query Editor and export or save the query for scheduled recurring analysis.

title: Validate ingested batch data quality
t1: Ingest a batch of customer records into an Experience Platform dataset via batch ingestion.
t2: Open Query Service and write a SQL query targeting the ingested dataset to check field values and row counts.
t3: Run the query and review the results to identify null values, duplicates, or unexpected field distributions.
t4: Use the query findings to confirm data quality or flag issues before enabling the dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile.

title: Behavioral events to high-value dataset
t1: Ingest raw behavioral event data into Experience Platform and confirm it lands in a queryable dataset.
t2: Write a SQL query in Query Service that aggregates event data to identify high-value customers by spend or engagement metrics.
t3: Execute the query as a CTAS statement to materialize the results into a new derived dataset in Platform.
t4: Enable the derived dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile so high-value customer attributes are available for segmentation and activation.

title: Query Service to Tableau audience dashboard
t1: Retrieve your Query Service credentials from the Experience Platform UI to enable external client connections.
t2: Connect Tableau Desktop to Query Service using the retrieved credentials and PostgreSQL connector.
t3: Write and run SQL queries in Tableau to pull audience membership and engagement data from Platform datasets.
t4: Build an interactive audience performance visualization in Tableau using the queried data.

title: SQL query to re-engage lapsed buyers
t1: Open Query Service and write a SQL query that joins purchase event data with customer profiles to find all customers.
t2: Filter the query results to return only customers whose last purchase date is more than 30 days ago.
t3: Save the query results as a new derived dataset containing the lapsed customer IDs.
t4: Use that derived dataset to build an audience in Segment Builder and activate it to a re-engagement destination.

title: Churn feature dataset from event history
t1: Connect to Query Service and explore the raw event history dataset to understand the available behavioral signals.
t2: Write and run SQL queries in Query Service to compute churn-indicator features such as days since last activity and session frequency.
t3: Save the query output as a new derived dataset in Experience Platform by using the CREATE TABLE AS SELECT statement.
t4: Enable the derived churn-indicator dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile so the features are available for segmentation and AI models.

title: Validate streaming events against XDM schema
t1: Configure a streaming source connector to ingest real-time events into an Experience Platform dataset mapped to your XDM schema.
t2: Allow the streaming ingestion to run until a representative set of events has landed in the dataset.
t3: Open Query Service and write a SQL query against the dataset to inspect field names, data types, and null counts across the ingested events.
t4: Compare the query results against the expected XDM schema definition to confirm all fields are correctly mapped and no schema violations exist.

title: Label restricted third-party schema fields
t1: Identify the contractually restricted third-party data fields in your existing XDM schema.
t2: Apply the appropriate DULE data usage labels to those schema fields to mark them as restricted.
t3: Create a data usage policy that references those labels to enforce contractual restrictions on downstream use.
t4: Verify that the policy triggers a violation warning when restricted fields are activated to a disallowed destination.

title: Label PII fields in profile schema
t1: Open an existing profile schema in the Schema Editor and identify fields that contain personally identifiable information such as name, email, and phone number.
t2: Apply the appropriate data usage labels, such as I1 or I2, to each identified PII field to mark them as sensitive personal data.
t3: Save the labeled schema so that the applied labels are propagated to any datasets created from that schema.
t4: Create a data usage policy that references those sensitivity labels to enforce restrictions on how those PII fields can be used or activated.

title: Label device fields to restrict identity stitching
t1: Open an existing XDM event schema in the Schema Editor and locate the device ID fields used for identity stitching.
t2: Apply appropriate data usage labels, such as I1 or I2, to those device ID fields to mark them as identity-linked and restricted.
t3: Create a data usage policy that references those labels and prohibits their use in identity-stitching operations across datasets.
t4: Enforce the policy so that any attempt to stitch profiles using the labeled device ID fields is blocked and flagged for review.

title: Label fields and block ad network exports
t1: Identify sensitive schema fields in your dataset that must not be shared with advertising platforms.
t2: Apply restrictive data usage labels to those schema fields to mark them as restricted for advertising.
t3: Create a data usage policy that references those labels and defines the prohibited marketing action of exporting to ad networks.
t4: Enable the policy so that Platform enforces it and blocks any activation of those labeled fields to advertising destinations.

title: Block health data from social media
t1: Apply sensitive health data usage labels to the relevant schema fields containing personal health information.
t2: Define a marketing action representing activation to social media advertising destinations.
t3: Create a data usage policy that restricts fields carrying health labels from being used with that marketing action.
t4: Enforce the policy so that any attempt to activate health-labeled data to social media destinations is automatically blocked.

title: Policy blocks restricted audience at activation
t1: Apply restrictive data usage labels to schema fields containing sensitive personal data.
t2: Create a data usage policy that prohibits activation of those labeled fields to advertising destinations.
t3: Build an audience segment that incorporates the restricted labeled fields from the schema.
t4: Attempt to activate the audience to an advertising destination and confirm the governance policy automatically blocks it.

title: Label, policy, and enforce at destination
t1: Apply data usage labels to sensitive schema fields to classify them as restricted for advertising use.
t2: Create a data usage policy that blocks activation of those labeled fields to advertising destinations.
t3: Attempt to activate an audience containing the labeled fields to an ad destination to trigger policy evaluation.
t4: Review the policy violation alert that blocks the activation, confirming governance enforcement is working correctly.

title: Healthcare data governance end to end
t1: Apply HIPAA-aligned data usage labels to sensitive health-related schema fields to mark them as restricted for marketing use.
t2: Create data usage policies that block those labeled fields from being activated to advertising or third-party marketing destinations.
t3: Build a compliant audience using only unlabeled or permitted fields in Segment Builder, respecting all governance constraints.
t4: Activate the audience to an approved healthcare marketing destination, allowing Platform to enforce policies and block any violations.

title: GDPR access request to data export
t1: Submit a GDPR data access request through the Privacy Service API or UI, specifying the customer's identity.
t2: Privacy Service fans out the request to all configured Experience Platform products and data stores holding that customer's data.
t3: Each product retrieves the matching records and packages them into a downloadable data file.
t4: Download and deliver the compiled data export to the customer to fulfill the GDPR access request.

title: Erase customer data via CCPA request
t1: Submit a CCPA deletion job through Privacy Service API or UI, specifying the customer's identity values to target their data.
t2: Privacy Service validates the request and fans it out to all connected Platform services that hold the customer's data.
t3: Each Platform service locates and deletes the customer's data records tied to the submitted identities.
t4: Privacy Service marks the job as complete and returns a confirmation so you can document compliance with the deletion request.

title: Collect and forward website opt-out signals
t1: Install the AEP Privacy JavaScript library on your website by adding the script tag to your page.
t2: Configure the library with your organization ID so it can route consent signals to the correct Experience Cloud solutions.
t3: Capture visitor opt-out interactions on your website and pass them to the library's opt-out API.
t4: The library forwards the opt-out signals to Privacy Service, which propagates the consent preferences across all connected AEP solutions.

title: Automate Privacy Requests via REST API
t1: Authenticate with the Privacy Service API by obtaining an access token using your IMS organization credentials.
t2: Submit bulk privacy job requests by sending POST calls to the API with customer identity details and regulation type.
t3: Poll the API with the returned job IDs to monitor processing status until all privacy jobs reach completion.
t4: Retrieve the completed job results from the API and confirm that the requested data access or deletion has been fulfilled.

title: Monitor deletion requests via event subscription
t1: Register an Adobe I/O integration and configure a webhook endpoint to receive Privacy Service event notifications.
t2: Subscribe the integration to Privacy Service events so job completion notifications are routed to your webhook.
t3: Submit a GDPR or CCPA deletion request through the Privacy Service API to initiate the deletion job.
t4: Receive the real-time job completion event at your webhook and confirm the deletion request was fulfilled.

title: Subscribe to segment job failure alert
t1: Navigate to the Alerts section in Experience Platform and browse the available alert types.
t2: Select the segment job failure alert type to monitor audience evaluation errors.
t3: Subscribe to the alert by entering your notification preferences, such as email or in-platform notifications.
t4: Receive an immediate notification when an audience evaluation job fails so you can investigate and resolve the issue.

title: Monitor daily pipeline with ingestion alert
t1: Navigate to the Alerts section in Experience Platform and browse the available alert rules.
t2: Select the ingestion delay metric alert rule that matches your critical daily data pipeline.
t3: Configure the alert threshold and notification channel, then enable the alert rule.
t4: Receive a notification when ingestion delay exceeds the threshold, confirming the pipeline is actively monitored.

title: Alert for destination activation failure
t1: Connect your high-priority campaign destination in Experience Platform to ensure it is ready to receive audience activations.
t2: Activate your high-priority campaign audience to that connected destination to initiate the data flow.
t3: Navigate to the Alerts section in Experience Platform and subscribe to the destination activation failure alert type.
t4: Receive an immediate notification if the activation fails so your team can investigate and resolve the issue quickly.

title: Monitor batch ingestion job success
t1: Ingest a batch of customer data into an Experience Platform dataset using batch ingestion.
t2: Navigate to the Monitoring dashboard in the Platform UI to locate the ingestion job.
t3: Open the batch run details to review the number of records ingested and any failed records.
t4: Confirm the batch status shows as Success before proceeding with downstream processing.

title: Monitor audience activation to ad destination
t1: Build a new audience in Segment Builder and publish it to make it available for activation.
t2: Connect an advertising destination and activate the published audience to that destination.
t3: Navigate to the Monitoring dashboard and open the Segment Activation view to find the active dataflow.
t4: Review the dataflow run details, checking ingested identity counts and any errors to confirm successful delivery.

title: Diagnose missing records in source dataflow
t1: Navigate to the Sources catalog in Experience Platform and open the active source connection you want to investigate.
t2: Open the Dataflows tab for that source connection to view the list of recent dataflow runs and their statuses.
t3: Select a failed or partial dataflow run to inspect its detailed run history, including ingested record counts and error messages.
t4: Use the error codes and failed-record details surfaced in the run report to identify and resolve the root cause of the missing records.

title: Grant team member AI Assistant access
t1: Open the Admin Console and confirm the team member has been added as a user in the organization.
t2: Navigate to the Permissions UI and open the role assigned to that team member.
t3: Add the AI Assistant access and AI Assistant Operational Insights permissions to that role.
t4: Save the updated role so the team member can now access AI Assistant in Experience Platform.

title: Learn merge policies via AI Assistant
t1: Ask AI Assistant to explain what merge policies are and how they control which data fragments are prioritized in a unified profile.
t2: Ask AI Assistant to describe the difference between timestamp-ordered and custom attribute precedence merge strategies.
t3: Ask AI Assistant how selecting a specific merge policy affects the attributes and identities returned during a Real-Time Customer Profile lookup.
t4: Use the AI Assistant's explanations to configure the appropriate merge policy for your dataset and validate profile lookups return the expected data.

title: AI-guided audience destination activation
t1: Open AI Assistant and ask it for a step-by-step guide on activating an audience to a new destination.
t2: Follow the AI Assistant's instructions to navigate to Destinations and configure a new destination connection.
t3: Use the guidance provided to select your target audience and map the required identity and attribute fields.
t4: Complete the activation flow as directed by AI Assistant to start delivering your audience to the new destination.

title: Troubleshoot streaming segment evaluation failure
t1: Ask AI Assistant why your streaming segment is not evaluating in real time and describe the observed behavior.
t2: Review AI Assistant's explanation of common causes such as missing streaming ingestion setup or unsupported segment operators.
t3: Follow AI Assistant's guided steps to verify that the source dataset is streaming-enabled and the segment criteria support streaming evaluation.
t4: Confirm the fix by monitoring the segment evaluation logs and asking AI Assistant to validate the updated configuration.

title: Find empty audiences using AI Assistant
t1: Open AI Assistant in the Experience Platform UI within your sandbox environment.
t2: Ask AI Assistant how many audiences currently have zero profiles in this sandbox.
t3: AI Assistant queries operational metadata and returns the count of empty audiences with their names.
t4: Review the list of zero-profile audiences and take corrective action such as deleting or rebuilding them.

title: Find journeys using a specific audience
t1: Open AI Assistant in Journey Optimizer and confirm it is connected to your production sandbox.
t2: Ask AI Assistant which journeys are currently live and actively using your target audience by name.
t3: Review the list of journeys returned by AI Assistant, including their statuses and entry conditions referencing that audience.
t4: Use the journey names provided to navigate directly to each journey and take any necessary action.

title: Find and delete unused audiences
t1: Open AI Assistant in Experience Platform and ask it to list all audiences that have never been activated to any destination.
t2: Review the AI Assistant's response to confirm the full list of inactive audiences returned.
t3: Select each unused audience from the list in the Audiences UI to verify it is safe to remove.
t4: Delete the confirmed unused audiences to clean up the audience inventory and reduce clutter.

title: Identify and remove unused audiences
t1: Ask AI Assistant to list all audiences with zero profile counts in your sandbox.
t2: Review the returned list of empty audiences and confirm they are safe to delete before migration.
t3: Delete the identified zero-profile audiences to clean up the sandbox environment.
t4: Verify with AI Assistant that no unused audiences remain before proceeding with the sandbox migration.

title: Check dependencies before deleting schema attribute
t1: Identify the schema attribute you are considering deleting from your data model.
t2: Ask AI Assistant which datasets, segments, and journeys depend on that schema attribute.
t3: Review the full list of dependent objects returned by AI Assistant to assess the impact of deletion.
t4: Remove or update all dependent objects confirmed by AI Assistant before safely deleting the schema attribute.

title: Schema field change impact analysis
t1: Identify the schema field you plan to modify or remove in Experience Platform.
t2: Ask AI Assistant to trace the lineage of that field across datasets, segments, and journeys.
t3: Review the downstream assets AI Assistant surfaces that depend on the field, such as audiences and activated destinations.
